fields.description: Determines whether the pass is limited to a one-time use. If true, the pass can be used once; if false, the pass can be used multiple times within the Temporary Access Pass lifetime.

fields.name: lifetimeInMinutes
fields.description: The lifetime of the Temporary Access Pass in minutes starting at startDateTime. Must be between 10 and 43200 inclusive (equivalent to 30 days).

fields.name: methodUsabilityReason
fields.description: Details about the usability state (isUsable). Reasons can include: EnabledByPolicy, DisabledByPolicy, Expired, NotYetValid, OneTimeUsed.

fields.name: startDateTime
fields.description: The date and time when the Temporary Access Pass becomes available to use and when isUsable is true is enforced.

fields.name: temporaryAccessPass
fields.description: The Temporary Access Pass used to authenticate. Returned only on creation of a new temporaryAccessPassAuthenticationMethod object; Hidden in subsequent read operations and returned as null with GET.

fields.name: createdDateTime
fields.description: Date and time of term creation. Read-only.

fields.name: descriptions
fields.description: Description about term that is dependent on the languageTag.

fields.name: labels
fields.description: Label metadata for a term.

fields.name: lastModifiedDateTime
fields.description: Last date and time of term modification. Read-only.

fields.name: properties
fields.description: Collection of properties on the term.

fields.name: children
fields.description: Children of current term.

fields.name: relations
fields.description: To indicate which terms are related to the current term as either pinned or reused.

fields.name: allowMultipleValues
fields.description: Specifies whether the column allows more than one value.

fields.name: showFullyQualifiedName
fields.description: Specifies whether to display the entire term path or only the term label.

fields.name: description
fields.description: The description in the localized language.

fields.name: languageTag
fields.description: The language tag for the label.

fields.name: isDefault
fields.description: Indicates whether the label is the default label.

fields.name: languageTag
fields.description: The language tag for the label.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The name of the label.

fields.name: languageTag
fields.description: The language tag for the label.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The name in the localized language.

fields.name: allowMultipleLines
fields.description: Whether to allow multiple lines of text.

fields.name: appendChangesToExistingText
fields.description: Whether updates to this column should replace existing text, or append to it.

fields.name: linesForEditing
fields.description: The size of the text box.

fields.name: maxLength
fields.description: The maximum number of characters for the value.

fields.name: textType
fields.description: The type of text being stored. Must be one of plain or richText

fields.name: content
fields.description: The content stream for the thumbnail.

fields.name: height
fields.description: The height of the thumbnail, in pixels.

fields.name: sourceItemId
fields.description: The unique identifier of the item that provided the thumbnail. This is only available when a folder thumbnail is requested.

fields.name: url
fields.description: The URL used to fetch the thumbnail content.

fields.name: width
fields.description: The width of the thumbnail, in pixels.

fields.name: breaks
fields.description: The list of breaks associated with the timeCard.

fields.name: userId
fields.description: User ID to which the timeCard belongs.

fields.name: breakId
fields.description: ID of the timeCardBreak.

fields.name: breaks
fields.description: The clock-in event of the timeCard.

fields.name: dateTime
fields.description: The time the entry is recorded.

fields.name: isAtApprovedLocation
fields.description: Indicates whether this action happens at an approved location.

fields.name: isStagedForDeletion
fields.description: The timeOff is marked for deletion, a process that is finalized when the schedule is shared.

fields.name: userId
fields.description: ID of the user assigned to the timeOff. Required.

fields.name: timeOffReasonId
fields.description: ID of the timeOffReason for this timeOffItem. Required.

fields.name: code
fields.description: The code of the timeOffReason to represent an external identifier. This field must be unique within the team in Microsoft Teams and uses an alphanumeric format, with a maximum of 100 characters.

fields.name: displayName
fields.description: The name of the timeOffReason. Required.

fields.name: isActive
fields.description: Indicates whether the timeOffReason can be used when creating new entities or updating existing ones. Required.

fields.name: endDateTime
fields.description: The date and time the time off ends in ISO 8601 format and in UTC time.

fields.name: startDateTime
fields.description: The date and time the time off starts in ISO 8601 format and in UTC time.

fields.name: timeOffReasonId
fields.description: The reason for the time off.

fields.name: endTime
fields.description: End time for the time range.

fields.name: startTime
fields.description: Start time for the time range.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The name of a time zone. It can be a standard time zone name such as 'Hawaii-Aleutian Standard Time', or 'Customized Time Zone' for a custom time zone.

fields.name: lists
fields.description: The task lists in the users mailbox.

fields.name: bodyLastModifiedDateTime
fields.description: The date and time when the task body was last modified. By default, it is in UTC. You can provide a custom time zone in the request header. The property value uses ISO 8601 format and is always in UTC time. For example, midnight UTC on Jan 1, 2020 would look like this: '2020-01-01T00:00:00Z'.

fields.name: categories
fields.description: The categories associated with the task. Each category corresponds to the displayName property of an outlookCategory that the user has defined.

fields.name: createdDateTime
fields.description: The date and time when the task was created. By default, it is in UTC. You can provide a custom time zone in the request header. The property value uses ISO 8601 format. For example, midnight UTC on Jan 1, 2020 would look like this: '2020-01-01T00:00:00Z'.

fields.name: hasAttachments
fields.description: Indicates whether the task has attachments.

fields.name: isReminderOn
fields.description: Set to true if an alert is set to remind the user of the task.

fields.name: lastModifiedDateTime
fields.description: The date and time when the task was last modified. By default, it is in UTC. You can provide a custom time zone in the request header. The property value uses ISO 8601 format and is always in UTC time. For example, midnight UTC on Jan 1, 2020 would look like this: '2020-01-01T00:00:00Z'.

fields.name: title
fields.description: A brief description of the task.

fields.name: attachments
fields.description: A collection of file attachments for the task.

fields.name: checklistItems
fields.description: A collection of checklistItems linked to a task.

fields.name: extensions
fields.description: The collection of open extensions defined for the task. Nullable.

fields.name: linkedResources
fields.description: A collection of resources linked to the task.

fields.name: displayName
fields.description: The name of the task list.

fields.name: isOwner
fields.description: True if the user is owner of the given task list.

fields.name: isShared
fields.description: True if the task list is shared with other users

fields.name: extensions
fields.description: The collection of open extensions defined for the task list. Nullable.

fields.name: tasks
fields.description: The tasks in this task list. Read-only. Nullable.

fields.name: lastModifiedDateTime
fields.description: The Timestamp type represents date and time information using ISO 8601 format and is always in UTC time. For example, midnight UTC on Jan 1, 2014 is 2014-01-01T00:00:00Z

fields.name: weight
fields.description: Value indicating how much the document is currently trending. The larger the number, the more the document is currently trending around the user (the more relevant it is). Returned documents are sorted by this value.

fields.name: expirationDateTime
fields.description: The date and time in UTC that the upload session expires. The complete file must be uploaded before this expiration time is reached. Each fragment uploaded during the session extends the expiration time.

fields.name: nextExpectedRanges
fields.description: A collection of byte ranges that the server is missing for the file. These ranges are zero indexed and of the format 'start-end' (for example '0-26' to indicate the first 27 bytes of the file). When uploading files as Outlook attachments, instead of a collection of ranges, this property always indicates a single value '{start}', the location in the file where the next upload should begin.

fields.name: uploadUrl
fields.description: The URL endpoint that accepts PUT requests for byte ranges of the file.

fields.name: lastAccessedDateTime
fields.description: The date and time the resource was last accessed by the user. The timestamp represents date and time information using ISO 8601 format and is always in UTC time. For example, midnight UTC on Jan 1, 2014 is 2014-01-01T00:00:00Z. Read-only.

fields.name: lastModifiedDateTime
fields.description: The date and time the resource was last modified by the user. The timestamp represents date and time information using ISO 8601 format and is always in UTC time. For example, midnight UTC on Jan 1, 2014 is 2014-01-01T00:00:00Z. Read-only.

fields.name: ownerEmail
fields.description: The email of owner label rights.

fields.name: userEmail
fields.description: The email of user with label user rights.

fields.name: aboutMe
fields.description: A freeform text entry field for the user to describe themselves. Returned only on $select.

fields.name: accountEnabled
fields.description: true if the account is enabled; otherwise, false. This property is required when a user is created. Returned only on $select. Supports $filter (eq, ne, not, and in).

fields.name: ageGroup
fields.description: Sets the age group of the user. Allowed values: null, Minor, NotAdult, and Adult. For more information, see legal age group property definitions. Returned only on $select. Supports $filter (eq, ne, not, and in).

fields.name: assignedLicenses
fields.description: The licenses that are assigned to the user, including inherited (group-based) licenses. This property doesn't differentiate between directly assigned and inherited licenses. Use the licenseAssignmentStates property to identify the directly assigned and inherited licenses. Not nullable. Returned only on $select. Supports $filter (eq, not, /$count eq 0, /$count ne 0).

fields.name: assignedPlans
fields.description: The plans that are assigned to the user. Read-only. Not nullable. Returned only on $select. Supports $filter (eq and not).

fields.name: birthday
fields.description: The birthday of the user. The Timestamp type represents date and time information using ISO 8601 format and is always in UTC. For example, midnight UTC on Jan 1, 2014, is 2014-01-01T00:00:00Z. Returned only on $select.

fields.name: businessPhones
fields.description: The telephone numbers for the user. NOTE: Although it's a string collection, only one number can be set for this property. Read-only for users synced from the on-premises directory. Returned by default. Supports $filter (eq, not, ge, le, startsWith).

fields.name: city
fields.description: The city where the user is located. Maximum length is 128 characters. Returned only on $select. Supports $filter (eq, ne, not, ge, le, in, startsWith, and eq on null values).

fields.name: companyName
fields.description: The name of the company that the user is associated with. This property can be useful for describing the company that a guest comes from. The maximum length is 64 characters.Returned only on $select. Supports $filter (eq, ne, not, ge, le, in, startsWith, and eq on null values).

fields.name: consentProvidedForMinor
fields.description: Sets whether consent was obtained for minors. Allowed values: null, Granted, Denied, and NotRequired. For more information, see legal age group property definitions. Returned only on $select. Supports $filter (eq, ne, not, and in).

fields.name: country
fields.description: The country or region where the user is located; for example, US or UK. Maximum length is 128 characters. Returned only on $select. Supports $filter (eq, ne, not, ge, le, in, startsWith, and eq on null values).

fields.name: createdDateTime
fields.description: The date and time the user was created, in ISO 8601 format and UTC. The value can't be modified and is automatically populated when the entity is created. Nullable. For on-premises users, the value represents when they were first created in Microsoft Entra ID. Property is null for some users created before June 2018 and on-premises users that were synced to Microsoft Entra ID before June 2018. Read-only. Returned only on $select. Supports $filter (eq, ne, not , ge, le, in).

fields.name: creationType
fields.description: Indicates whether the user account was created through one of the following methods:  As a regular school or work account (null). As an external account (Invitation). As a local account for an Azure Active Directory B2C tenant (LocalAccount). Through self-service sign-up by an internal user using email verification (EmailVerified). Through self-service sign-up by a guest signing up through a link that is part of a user flow (SelfServiceSignUp). Read-only.Returned only on $select. Supports $filter (eq, ne, not, in).

fields.name: department
fields.description: The name of the department in which the user works. Maximum length is 64 characters. Returned only on $select. Supports $filter (eq, ne, not , ge, le, in, and eq on null values).

fields.name: deviceEnrollmentLimit
fields.description: The limit on the maximum number of devices that the user is permitted to enroll. Allowed values are 5 or 1000.

fields.name: displayName
fields.description: The name displayed in the address book for the user. This value is usually the combination of the user's first name, middle initial, and family name. This property is required when a user is created and it can't be cleared during updates. Maximum length is 256 characters. Returned by default. Supports $filter (eq, ne, not , ge, le, in, startsWith, and eq on null values), $orderby, and $search.

fields.name: employeeHireDate
fields.description: The date and time when the user was hired or will start work in a future hire. Returned only on $select. Supports $filter (eq, ne, not , ge, le, in).

fields.name: employeeId
fields.description: The employee identifier assigned to the user by the organization. The maximum length is 16 characters. Returned only on $select. Supports $filter (eq, ne, not , ge, le, in, startsWith, and eq on null values).

fields.name: employeeLeaveDateTime
fields.description: The date and time when the user left or will leave the organization. To read this property, the calling app must be assigned the User-LifeCycleInfo.Read.All permission. To write this property, the calling app must be assigned the User.Read.All and User-LifeCycleInfo.ReadWrite.All permissions. To read this property in delegated scenarios, the admin needs at least one of the following Microsoft Entra roles: Lifecycle Workflows Administrator (least privilege), Global Reader. To write this property in delegated scenarios, the admin needs the Global Administrator role. Supports $filter (eq, ne, not , ge, le, in). For more information, see Configure the employeeLeaveDateTime property for a user.

fields.name: employeeType
fields.description: Captures enterprise worker type. For example, Employee, Contractor, Consultant, or Vendor. Returned only on $select. Supports $filter (eq, ne, not , ge, le, in, startsWith).

fields.name: externalUserState
fields.description: For a guest invited to the tenant using the invitation API, this property represents the invited user's invitation status. For invited users, the state can be PendingAcceptance or Accepted, or null for all other users. Returned only on $select. Supports $filter (eq, ne, not , in).

fields.name: externalUserStateChangeDateTime
fields.description: Shows the timestamp for the latest change to the externalUserState property. Returned only on $select. Supports $filter (eq, ne, not , in).

fields.name: faxNumber
fields.description: The fax number of the user. Returned only on $select. Supports $filter (eq, ne, not , ge, le, in, startsWith, and eq on null values).

fields.name: givenName
fields.description: The given name (first name) of the user. Maximum length is 64 characters. Returned by default. Supports $filter (eq, ne, not , ge, le, in, startsWith, and eq on null values).

fields.name: hireDate
fields.description: The hire date of the user. The Timestamp type represents date and time information using ISO 8601 format and is always in UTC. For example, midnight UTC on Jan 1, 2014, is 2014-01-01T00:00:00Z. Returned only on $select.  Note: This property is specific to SharePoint in Microsoft 365. We recommend using the native employeeHireDate property to set and update hire date values using Microsoft Graph APIs.

fields.name: identities
fields.description: Represents the identities that can be used to sign in to this user account. Microsoft (also known as a local account), organizations, or social identity providers such as Facebook, Google, and Microsoft can provide identity and tie it to a user account. It might contain multiple items with the same signInType value. Returned only on $select.  Supports $filter (eq) with limitations.

fields.name: imAddresses
fields.description: The instant message voice-over IP (VOIP) session initiation protocol (SIP) addresses for the user. Read-only. Returned only on $select. Supports $filter (eq, not, ge, le, startsWith).

fields.name: interests
fields.description: A list for the user to describe their interests. Returned only on $select.

fields.name: isManagementRestricted
fields.description: true if the user is a member of a restricted management administrative unit. If not set, the default value is null and the default behavior is false. Read-only.  To manage a user who is a member of a restricted management administrative unit, the administrator or calling app must be assigned a Microsoft Entra role at the scope of the restricted management administrative unit. Returned only on $select.

fields.name: isResourceAccount
fields.description: Don't use – reserved for future use.

fields.name: jobTitle
fields.description: The user's job title. Maximum length is 128 characters. Returned by default. Supports $filter (eq, ne, not , ge, le, in, startsWith, and eq on null values).

fields.name: lastPasswordChangeDateTime
fields.description: The time when this Microsoft Entra user last changed their password or when their password was created, whichever date the latest action was performed. The date and time information uses ISO 8601 format and is always in UTC. For example, midnight UTC on Jan 1, 2014 is 2014-01-01T00:00:00Z. Returned only on $select.

fields.name: legalAgeGroupClassification
fields.description: Used by enterprise applications to determine the legal age group of the user. This property is read-only and calculated based on ageGroup and consentProvidedForMinor properties. Allowed values: null, Undefined,  MinorWithOutParentalConsent, MinorWithParentalConsent, MinorNoParentalConsentRequired, NotAdult, and Adult. For more information, see legal age group property definitions. Returned only on $select.

fields.name: licenseAssignmentStates
fields.description: State of license assignments for this user. Also indicates licenses that are directly assigned or the user inherited through group memberships. Read-only. Returned only on $select.

fields.name: mail
fields.description: The SMTP address for the user, for example, jeff@contoso.com. Changes to this property update the user's proxyAddresses collection to include the value as an SMTP address. This property can't contain accent characters.  NOTE: We don't recommend updating this property for Azure AD B2C user profiles. Use the otherMails property instead. Returned by default. Supports $filter (eq, ne, not, ge, le, in, startsWith, endsWith, and eq on null values).

fields.name: mailNickname
fields.description: The mail alias for the user. This property must be specified when a user is created. Maximum length is 64 characters. Returned only on $select. Supports $filter (eq, ne, not, ge, le, in, startsWith, and eq on null values).

fields.name: mobilePhone
fields.description: The primary cellular telephone number for the user. Read-only for users synced from the on-premises directory. Maximum length is 64 characters. Returned by default. Supports $filter (eq, ne, not, ge, le, in, startsWith, and eq on null values) and $search.

fields.name: mySite
fields.description: The URL for the user's site. Returned only on $select.

fields.name: officeLocation
fields.description: The office location in the user's place of business. Returned by default. Supports $filter (eq, ne, not, ge, le, in, startsWith, and eq on null values).

fields.name: onPremisesDistinguishedName
fields.description: Contains the on-premises Active Directory distinguished name or DN. The property is only populated for customers who are synchronizing their on-premises directory to Microsoft Entra ID via Microsoft Entra Connect. Read-only. Returned only on $select.

fields.name: onPremisesDomainName
fields.description: Contains the on-premises domainFQDN, also called dnsDomainName synchronized from the on-premises directory. The property is only populated for customers who are synchronizing their on-premises directory to Microsoft Entra ID via Microsoft Entra Connect. Read-only. Returned only on $select.

fields.name: onPremisesImmutableId
fields.description: This property is used to associate an on-premises Active Directory user account to their Microsoft Entra user object. This property must be specified when creating a new user account in the Graph if you're using a federated domain for the user's userPrincipalName (UPN) property. NOTE: The $ and _ characters can't be used when specifying this property. Returned only on $select. Supports $filter (eq, ne, not, ge, le, in).

fields.name: onPremisesLastSyncDateTime
fields.description: Indicates the last time at which the object was synced with the on-premises directory; for example: 2013-02-16T03:04:54Z. The Timestamp type represents date and time information using ISO 8601 format and is always in UTC. For example, midnight UTC on Jan 1, 2014 is 2014-01-01T00:00:00Z. Read-only. Returned only on $select. Supports $filter (eq, ne, not, ge, le, in).

fields.name: onPremisesProvisioningErrors
fields.description: Errors when using Microsoft synchronization product during provisioning. Returned only on $select. Supports $filter (eq, not, ge, le).

fields.name: onPremisesSamAccountName
fields.description: Contains the on-premises samAccountName synchronized from the on-premises directory. The property is only populated for customers who are synchronizing their on-premises directory to Microsoft Entra ID via Microsoft Entra Connect. Read-only. Returned only on $select. Supports $filter (eq, ne, not, ge, le, in, startsWith).

fields.name: onPremisesSecurityIdentifier
fields.description: Contains the on-premises security identifier (SID) for the user that was synchronized from on-premises to the cloud. Read-only. Returned only on $select. Supports $filter (eq including on null values).

fields.name: onPremisesSyncEnabled
fields.description: true if this user object is currently being synced from an on-premises Active Directory (AD); otherwise the user isn't being synced and can be managed in Microsoft Entra ID. Read-only. Returned only on $select. Supports $filter (eq, ne, not, in, and eq on null values).

fields.name: onPremisesUserPrincipalName
fields.description: Contains the on-premises userPrincipalName synchronized from the on-premises directory. The property is only populated for customers who are synchronizing their on-premises directory to Microsoft Entra ID via Microsoft Entra Connect. Read-only. Returned only on $select. Supports $filter (eq, ne, not, ge, le, in, startsWith).

fields.name: otherMails
fields.description: A list of other email addresses for the user; for example: ['bob@contoso.com', 'Robert@fabrikam.com']. Can store up to 250 values, each with a limit of 250 characters. NOTE: This property can't contain accent characters. Returned only on $select. Supports $filter (eq, not, ge, le, in, startsWith, endsWith, /$count eq 0, /$count ne 0).

fields.name: passwordPolicies
fields.description: Specifies password policies for the user. This value is an enumeration with one possible value being DisableStrongPassword, which allows weaker passwords than the default policy to be specified. DisablePasswordExpiration can also be specified. The two might be specified together; for example: DisablePasswordExpiration, DisableStrongPassword. Returned only on $select. For more information on the default password policies, see Microsoft Entra password policies. Supports $filter (ne, not, and eq on null values).

fields.name: pastProjects
fields.description: A list for the user to enumerate their past projects. Returned only on $select.

fields.name: postalCode
fields.description: The postal code for the user's postal address. The postal code is specific to the user's country or region. In the United States of America, this attribute contains the ZIP code. Maximum length is 40 characters. Returned only on $select. Supports $filter (eq, ne, not, ge, le, in, startsWith, and eq on null values).

fields.name: preferredDataLocation
fields.description: The preferred data location for the user. For more information, see OneDrive Online Multi-Geo.

fields.name: preferredLanguage
fields.description: The preferred language for the user. The preferred language format is based on RFC 4646. The name is a combination of an ISO 639 two-letter lowercase culture code associated with the language, and an ISO 3166 two-letter uppercase subculture code associated with the country or region. Example: 'en-US', or 'es-ES'. Returned by default. Supports $filter (eq, ne, not, ge, le, in, startsWith, and eq on null values)

fields.name: preferredName
fields.description: The preferred name for the user. Not Supported. This attribute returns an empty string.Returned only on $select.

fields.name: provisionedPlans
fields.description: The plans that are provisioned for the user. Read-only. Not nullable. Returned only on $select. Supports $filter (eq, not, ge, le).

fields.name: proxyAddresses
fields.description: For example: ['SMTP: bob@contoso.com', 'smtp: bob@sales.contoso.com']. Changes to the mail property update this collection to include the value as an SMTP address. For more information, see mail and proxyAddresses properties. The proxy address prefixed with SMTP (capitalized) is the primary proxy address, while those addresses prefixed with smtp are the secondary proxy addresses. For Azure AD B2C accounts, this property has a limit of 10 unique addresses. Read-only in Microsoft Graph; you can update this property only through the Microsoft 365 admin center. Not nullable. Returned only on $select. Supports $filter (eq, not, ge, le, startsWith, endsWith, /$count eq 0, /$count ne 0).

fields.name: responsibilities
fields.description: A list for the user to enumerate their responsibilities. Returned only on $select.

fields.name: schools
fields.description: A list for the user to enumerate the schools they attended. Returned only on $select.

fields.name: securityIdentifier
fields.description: Security identifier (SID) of the user, used in Windows scenarios. Read-only. Returned by default. Supports $select and $filter (eq, not, ge, le, startsWith).

fields.name: serviceProvisioningErrors
fields.description: Errors published by a federated service describing a nontransient, service-specific error regarding the properties or link from a user object.  Supports $filter (eq, not, for isResolved and serviceInstance).

fields.name: showInAddressList
fields.description: Do not use in Microsoft Graph. Manage this property through the Microsoft 365 admin center instead. Represents whether the user should be included in the Outlook global address list. See Known issue.

fields.name: signInSessionsValidFromDateTime
fields.description: Any refresh tokens or session tokens (session cookies) issued before this time are invalid. Applications get an error when using an invalid refresh or session token to acquire a delegated access token (to access APIs such as Microsoft Graph). If this happens, the application needs to acquire a new refresh token by requesting the authorized endpoint. Read-only. Use revokeSignInSessions to reset. Returned only on $select.

fields.name: skills
fields.description: A list for the user to enumerate their skills. Returned only on $select.

fields.name: state
fields.description: The state or province in the user's address. Maximum length is 128 characters. Returned only on $select. Supports $filter (eq, ne, not, ge, le, in, startsWith, and eq on null values).

fields.name: streetAddress
fields.description: The street address of the user's place of business. Maximum length is 1,024 characters. Returned only on $select. Supports $filter (eq, ne, not, ge, le, in, startsWith, and eq on null values).

fields.name: surname
fields.description: The user's surname (family name or last name). Maximum length is 64 characters. Returned by default. Supports $filter (eq, ne, not, ge, le, in, startsWith, and eq on null values).

fields.name: usageLocation
fields.description: A two-letter country code (ISO standard 3166). Required for users that are assigned licenses due to legal requirements to check for availability of services in countries/regions. Examples include: US, JP, and GB. Not nullable. Returned only on $select. Supports $filter (eq, ne, not, ge, le, in, startsWith, and eq on null values).

fields.name: userPrincipalName
fields.description: The user principal name (UPN) of the user. The UPN is an Internet-style sign-in name for the user based on the Internet standard RFC 822. By convention, this value should map to the user's email name. The general format is alias@domain, where the domain must be present in the tenant's collection of verified domains. This property is required when a user is created. The verified domains for the tenant can be accessed from the verifiedDomains property of organization.NOTE: This property can't contain accent characters. Only the following characters are allowed A - Z, a - z, 0 - 9, ' . - _ ! # ^ ~. For the complete list of allowed characters, see username policies. Returned by default. Supports $filter (eq, ne, not, ge, le, in, startsWith, endsWith) and $orderby.

fields.name: userType
fields.description: A string value that can be used to classify user types in your directory. The possible values are Member and Guest. Returned only on $select. Supports $filter (eq, ne, not, in, and eq on null values). NOTE: For more information about the permissions for members and guests, see What are the default user permissions in Microsoft Entra ID?

fields.name: activities
fields.description: The user's activities across devices. Read-only. Nullable.

fields.name: agreementAcceptances
fields.description: The user's terms of use acceptance statuses. Read-only. Nullable.

fields.name: appRoleAssignments
fields.description: Represents the app roles a user is granted for an application. Supports $expand.

fields.name: calendarGroups
fields.description: The user's calendar groups. Read-only. Nullable.

URL for the domain representing the cross-platform identity mapping for the app. Mapping is stored either as a JSON file hosted on the domain or configurable via Windows Dev Center. The JSON file is named cross-platform-app-identifiers and is hosted at root of your HTTPS domain, either at the top level domain or include a sub domain. For example: https://contoso.com or https://myapp.contoso.com but NOT https://myapp.contoso.com/somepath. You must have a unique file and domain (or sub domain) per cross-platform app identity. name: ballerinax/aws.dynamodb
description: The Ballerina AWS DynamoDB connector provides the capability to programatically handle [AWS DynamoDB](hhttps://aws.amazon.com/dynamodb/) related operations.

fields.name: ArchivalBackupArn
fields.description:
The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the backup the table was archived to, when applicable in the 
archival reason. If you wish to restore this backup to the same table name, you will need to
delete the original table

fields.name: ArchivalDateTime
fields.description: The date and time when table archival was initiated by DynamoDB, in UNIX epoch time format

fields.name: ArchivalReason
fields.description:
The reason DynamoDB archived the table. Currently, the only possible value is:
INACCESSIBLE_ENCRYPTION_CREDENTIALS - The table was archived due to the table's AWS KMS key being
inaccessible for more than seven days. An On-Demand backup was created at the archival time

typeDefs.name: ArchivalSummary
typeDefs.description: Contains details of a table archival operation.

fields.name: AttributeName
fields.description: A name for the attribute

fields.name: AttributeType
fields.description:
The data type for the attribute, where: S - the attribute is of type String, N - the attribute is 
of type Number, B - the attribute is of type Binary

typeDefs.name: AttributeDefinition
typeDefs.description: Represents an attribute for describing the key schema for the table and indexes.

fields.name: B
fields.description: An attribute of type Binary

fields.name: BOOL
fields.description: An attribute of type Boolean

fields.name: BS
fields.description: An attribute of type Binary Set

fields.name: L
fields.description: An attribute of type List

fields.name: M
fields.description: An attribute of type Map

fields.name: N
fields.description: An attribute of type Number

fields.name: NS
fields.description: An attribute of type Number Set

fields.name: NULL
fields.description: An attribute of type Null

fields.name: S
fields.description: An attribute of type String

fields.name: SS
fields.description: An attribute of type String Set

typeDefs.name: AttributeValue
typeDefs.description:
Represents the data for an attribute. Each attribute value is described as a name-value pair. The name is the data
type, and the value is the data itself.

fields.name: Action
fields.description:
Speciﬁes how to perform the update. Valid values are PUT (default), DELETE, and ADD. The behavior depends
on whether the speciﬁed primary key already exists in the table

fields.name: Value
fields.description: Represents the data for an attribute

typeDefs.name: AttributeValueUpdate
typeDefs.description:
For the UpdateItem operation, represents the attributes to be modiﬁed, the action to perform on each, and the new
value for each.

fields.name: accessKeyId
fields.description: AWS access key

fields.name: secretAccessKey
fields.description: AWS secret key

typeDefs.name: AwsCredentials
typeDefs.description: Represents AWS credentials.

fields.name: accessKeyId
fields.description: AWS access key

fields.name: secretAccessKey
fields.description: AWS secret key

fields.name: securityToken
fields.description: AWS secret token

typeDefs.name: AwsTemporaryCredentials
typeDefs.description: Represents AWS temporary credentials.

fields.name: BackupName
fields.description: Name for the backup

fields.name: TableName
fields.description: Name of the table

typeDefs.name: BackupCreateInput
typeDefs.description: Represents an request to perform a CreateBackup operation on a table.

fields.name: BackupDetails
fields.description: Contains the details of the backup created for the table

fields.name: SourceTableDetails
fields.description: Contains the details of the table when the backup was created

fields.name: SourceTableFeatureDetails
fields.description: Contains the details of the features enabled on the table when the backup was created

typeDefs.name: BackupDescription
typeDefs.description: Represents a response after performing a CreateBackup operation on a table.

fields.name: BackupArn
fields.description: ARN associated with the backup

fields.name: BackupCreationDateTime
fields.description: Time at which the backup was created. This is the request time of the backup

fields.name: BackupName
fields.description: Name of the requested backup

fields.name: BackupStatus
fields.description: Backup can be in one of the following states: CREATING, ACTIVE, DELETED

fields.name: BackupType
fields.description: BackupType. One of USER, SYSTEM, AWS_BACKUP

fields.name: BackupExpiryDateTime
fields.description:
Time at which the automatic on-demand backup created by DynamoDB will expire. This SYSTEM on-demand backup 
expires automatically 35 days after its creation

fields.name: BackupSizeBytes
fields.description:
Size of the backup in bytes. DynamoDB updates this value approximately every six hours. Recent changes might
not be reflected in this value

typeDefs.name: BackupDetails
typeDefs.description: Contains the details of the backup created for the table.

fields.name: ConsumedCapacity
fields.description: The read capacity units consumed by the entire BatchGetItem operation

fields.name: TableName
fields.description: The name of the table containing the requested item

fields.name: Item
fields.description: The requested item

typeDefs.name: BatchItem
typeDefs.description: Represents ItemByBatchGet

fields.name: RequestItems
fields.description:
A map of one or more table names and, for each table, a map that describes one or more items to
retrieve from that table

fields.name: ReturnConsumedCapacity
fields.description:
Determines the level of detail about provisioned throughput consumption that is returned in
the response. Valid Values: INDEXES | TOTAL | NONE

typeDefs.name: BatchItemGetInput
typeDefs.description: Represents the request payload for a `BatchGetItem` operation.

fields.name: RequestItems
fields.description:
A map of one or more table names and, for each table, a list of operations to be performed
(DeleteRequest or PutRequest)

fields.name: ReturnConsumedCapacity
fields.description:
Determines the level of detail about provisioned throughput consumption that is returned
in the response. Valid Values: INDEXES | TOTAL | NONE

fields.name: ReturnItemCollectionMetrics
fields.description: Determines whether item collection metrics are returned. Valid Values: SIZE | NONE

typeDefs.name: BatchItemInsertInput
typeDefs.description: Represents the request payload `BatchWriteItem` operation.

fields.name: ConsumedCapacity
fields.description: The capacity units consumed by the entire `BatchWriteItem` operation

fields.name: ItemCollectionMetrics
fields.description:
A list of tables that were processed by `BatchWriteItem` and, for each table, information about
any item collections that were aﬀected by individual `DeleteItem` or  `PutItem` operations.

fields.name: UnprocessedItems
fields.description:
A map of tables and requests against those tables that were not processed. The `UnprocessedItems`
value is in the same form as `RequestItems`, so you can provide this value directly to a subsequent
`BatchGetItem` operation.

typeDefs.name: BatchItemInsertOutput
typeDefs.description: Represents the response after `WriteBatchItem` operation.

fields.name: BillingMode
fields.description:
Controls how you are charged for read and write throughput and how you manage capacity. This setting
can be changed later.
PROVISIONED - Sets the read/write capacity mode to PROVISIONED. We recommend using PROVISIONED for
predictable workloads.
PAY_PER_REQUEST - Sets the read/write capacity mode to PAY_PER_REQUEST. We recommend using
PAY_PER_REQUEST for unpredictable workloads.

fields.name: LastUpdateToPayPerRequestDateTime
fields.description: Represents the time when PAY_PER_REQUEST was last set as the read/write capacity mode

typeDefs.name: BillingModeSummary
typeDefs.description: Contains the details for the read/write capacity mode.

fields.name: CapacityUnits
fields.description: The total number of capacity units consumed on a table or an index

fields.name: ReadCapacityUnits
fields.description: The total number of read capacity units consumed on a table or an index

fields.name: WriteCapacityUnits
fields.description: The total number of write capacity units consumed on a table or an index

typeDefs.name: Capacity
typeDefs.description: Represents the amount of provisioned throughput capacity consumed on a table or an index.

fields.name: ComparisonOperator
fields.description:
A comparator for evaluating attributes. Valid Values: EQ | NE | IN | LE | LT | GE | GT |
BETWEEN | NOT_NULL | NULL | CONTAINS | NOT_CONTAINS | BEGINS_WITH

fields.name: AttributeValueList
fields.description:
One or more values to evaluate against the supplied attribute. The number of values in the list
depends on the ComparisonOperator being used

typeDefs.name: Condition
typeDefs.description:
Represents the selection criteria for a Query or Scan operation. For a Query operation, Condition is used for
specifying the KeyConditions to use when querying table or an index. For KeyConditions, only the following comparison
operators are supported: EQ | LE | LT | GE | GT | BEGINS_WITH | BETWEEN. For a Scan operation, Condition is used in a
ScanFilter, which evaluates the scan results and returns only the desired values

functions.name: createPlatformApplication
functions.description:
Creates a platform application object for one of the supported push notification services. You must specify 
`auth.platformPrincipal` and `auth.platformCredential` parameters.
- for `ADM` the `platformPrincipal` is the `client id` and `platformCredential` is the `client secret`
- for `APNS` and `APNS_SANDBOX` using certificate credentials, the `platformPrincipal` is the `SSL certificate` 
and `platformCredential` is the `private key`
- for `APNS` and `APNS_SANDBOX` using token credentials, the `platformPrincipal` is the `signing key ID` and the 
`platformCredential` is the `signing key` 
- for `FCM` there is no `platformPrincipal` and `platformCredential` is the `API key`
- for `BAIDU` the `platformPrincipal` is the `API key` and `platformCredential` is the `secret key`
- for `MPNS` the `platformPrincipal` is the `TLS certificate` and `platformCredential` is the `private key`
- for `WNS` the `platformPrincipal` is the `Package Security Identifier` and `platformCredential` is the 
`secret key`

parameters.description: The name of the platform application object to create

parameters.description: The platform of the application

parameters.description: Authentication credentials for the platform application

clients.name: Administrator
clients.description:
Ballerina Service Bus connector provides the capability to access Azure Service Bus SDK.
Service Bus API provides data access to highly reliable queues and publish/subscribe topics of Azure Service Bus with deep feature capabilities.

functions.name: init
functions.description:
Initialize the Azure Service Bus Admin client.
Create an [Azure account](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/learn/modules/create-an-azure-account/) and
obtain tokens following [this guide](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/service-bus-messaging/service-bus-quickstart-portal#get-the-connection-string).
Configure the connection string to have the [required permission](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/service-bus-messaging/service-bus-sas).
```ballerina
configurable string connectionString = ?;
asb:Administrator admin = check new (connectionString);
```

parameters.name: connectionString
parameters.description: Azure Service Bus connection string

functions.name: createTopic
functions.description:
Create a topic with the given name or name and options.
```ballerina
asb:TopicProperties? topicProperties = check admin->createTopic("topic-1");
```

parameters.name: topicName
parameters.description: Topic name

parameters.name: topicOptions
parameters.description: Topic options to create the topic.This should be a record of type CreateTopicOptions

functions.name: getTopic
functions.description:
Get the topic with the given name.
```ballerina
asb:TopicProperties? topicProperties = check admin->getTopic("topic-1");
```

parameters.name: topicName
parameters.description: Topic name

functions.name: updateTopic
functions.description:
Update the topic with the given options.
```ballerina
asb:TopicProperties? topicProp = check admin->updateTopic("topic-1", supportOrdering = true);
```

parameters.name: topicName
parameters.description: Topic name

parameters.name: topicOptions
parameters.description: Topic options to update the topic.This should be a record of type UpdateTopicOptions

functions.name: listTopics
functions.description:
List the topics.
```ballerina
asb:TopicList? topics = check admin->listTopics();
```

functions.name: deleteTopic
functions.description:
Delete the topic with the given name.
```ballerina
check admin->deleteTopic("topic-1");
```

parameters.name: topicName
parameters.description: Topic name

functions.name: createSubscription
functions.description:

members.name: SESSION_TRANSACTED
members.description:
Indicates that the session will use a local transaction which may subsequently 
be committed or rolled back by calling the session's `commit` or `rollback` methods.

members.name: AUTO_ACKNOWLEDGE
members.description:
Indicates that the session automatically acknowledges a client's receipt of a message 
either when the session has successfully returned from a call to `receive` or when 
the message listener the session has called to process the message successfully returns.

members.name: CLIENT_ACKNOWLEDGE
members.description:
Indicates that the client acknowledges a consumed message by calling the 
MessageConsumer's or Caller's `acknowledge` method. Acknowledging a consumed message 
acknowledges all messages that the session has consumed.

members.name: DUPS_OK_ACKNOWLEDGE
members.description:
Indicates that the session to lazily acknowledge the delivery of messages. 
This is likely to result in the delivery of some duplicate messages if the JMS provider fails, 
so it should only be used by consumers that can tolerate duplicate messages. 
Use of this mode can reduce session overhead by minimizing the work the session does to prevent duplicates.

functions.name: send
functions.description:
Sends a message to an IBM MQ topic.

This method supports JMS-compliant message delivery, including compatibility with
durable subscriptions and asynchronous message listeners.

Unlike the `put` method (which uses IBM MQ's native APIs), this method uses the JMS APIs and
is recommended for interoperability with JMS-based consumers.

```ballerina
check topic->send({payload: "Hello World".toBytes()});
```

parameters.description: The message to be sent to the topic.

return.description: An `ibmmq:Error` if the operation fails; otherwise, `()`

functions.name: query
functions.description:
Executes the query, which may return multiple results.
When processing the stream, make sure to consume all fetched data or close the stream.

parameters.name: sqlQuery
parameters.description: The SQL query such as `` `SELECT * from Album WHERE name=${albumName}` ``

parameters.name: rowType
parameters.description: The `typedesc` of the record to which the result needs to be returned

return.description: Stream of records in the `rowType` type

functions.name: queryRow
functions.description:
Executes the query, which is expected to return at most one row of the result.
If the query does not return any results, an `sql:NoRowsError` is returned.

parameters.name: sqlQuery
parameters.description: The SQL query such as `` `SELECT * from Album WHERE name=${albumName}` ``

parameters.name: returnType
parameters.description:
The `typedesc` of the record to which the result needs to be returned.
It can be a basic type if the query result contains only one column

return.description: Result in the `returnType` type or an `sql:Error`

functions.name: execute
functions.description: Executes the SQL query. Only the metadata of the execution is returned (not the results from the query).

parameters.name: sqlQuery
parameters.description: The SQL query such as `` `DELETE FROM Album WHERE artist=${artistName}` ``

return.description: Metadata of the query execution as an `sql:ExecutionResult` or an `sql:Error`

functions.name: batchExecute
functions.description:
Executes the SQL query with multiple sets of parameters in a batch. Only the metadata of the execution is returned (not results from the query).
If one of the commands in the batch fails, this will return an `sql:BatchExecuteError`. However, the driver may
or may not continue to process the remaining commands in the batch after a failure.

parameters.name: sqlQueries
parameters.description: The SQL query with multiple sets of parameters

return.description: Metadata of the query execution as an `sql:ExecutionResult[]` or an `sql:Error`

functions.name: call
functions.description:
Executes an SQL query, which calls a stored procedure. This may or may not
return results. Once the results are processed, the `close` method on `sql:ProcedureCallResult` must be called.

parameters.name: sqlQuery
parameters.description: The SQL query such as `` `CALL sp_GetAlbums();` ``

parameters.name: rowTypes
parameters.description: `typedesc` array of the records to which the results need to be returned

return.description: Summary of the execution and results are returned in an `sql:ProcedureCallResult`, or an `sql:Error`

functions.name: close
functions.description:
Closes the JDBC client and shuts down the connection pool. The client must be closed only at the end of the
application lifetime (or closed for graceful stops in a service).

return.description: Possible error when closing the client

clients.name: Caller
clients.description: Represents a Kafka caller, which can be used to commit the offsets consumed by the service.

functions.name: 'commit
functions.description:
Commits the currently consumed offsets of the service.
```ballerina
kafka:Error? result = caller->commit();
```

return.description: A `kafka:Error` if an error is encountered or else '()'

functions.name: commitOffset
functions.description:
Commits the given offsets and partitions for the given topics of the service.
```ballerina
kafka:Error? result = caller->commitOffset([partitionOffset1, partitionOffset2]);
```

parameters.name: offsets
parameters.description: Offsets to be committed

parameters.name: duration
parameters.description: Timeout duration (in seconds) for the commit operation execution

return.description: A `kafka:Error` if an error is encountered or else `()`

functions.name: seek
functions.description:
Seeks for a given offset in a topic partition.
```ballerina
kafka:Error? result = consumer->seek(partitionOffset);
```

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: The `PartitionOffset` to seek

return.description: A `kafka:Error` if an error is encountered or else `()`

clients.name: Consumer
clients.description: Represents a Kafka consumer endpoint.

parameters.name: bootstrapServers
parameters.description: List of remote server endpoints of Kafka brokers

parameters.name: config
parameters.description: Configurations related to the consumer endpoint

return.description: A `kafka:Error` if an error is encountered or else '()'

functions.name: assign
functions.description:
Assigns consumer to a set of topic partitions.
```ballerina
kafka:Error? result = consumer->assign([topicPartition1, topicPartition2]);
```

parameters.name: partitions
parameters.description: Topic partitions to be assigned

return.description: A `kafka:Error` if an error is encountered or else `()`

functions.name: close
functions.description:
Closes the consumer connection with the external Kafka broker.
```ballerina
kafka:Error? result = consumer->close();
```

parameters.name: duration
parameters.description: Timeout duration (in seconds) for the close operation execution

return.description: A `kafka:Error` if an error is encountered or else '()'

functions.name: 'commit
functions.description:
Commits the currently consumed offsets of the consumer.
```ballerina
kafka:Error? result = consumer->commit();
```

return.description: A `kafka:Error` if an error is encountered or else '()'

functions.name: commitOffset
functions.description:
Commits the given offsets of the specific topic partitions for the consumer.
```ballerina
kafka:Error? result = consumer->commitOffset([partitionOffset1, partitionOffset2]);
```

parameters.name: offsets
parameters.description: Offsets to be committed

parameters.name: duration
parameters.description: Timeout duration (in seconds) for the commit operation execution

return.description: A `kafka:Error` if an error is encountered or else `()`

functions.name: getAssignment
functions.description:
Retrieves the currently-assigned partitions of the consumer.
```ballerina
kafka:TopicPartition[] result = check consumer->getAssignment();
```

return.description: Array of assigned partitions for the consumer if executes successfully or else a `kafka:Error`

functions.name: getAvailableTopics
functions.description:
Retrieves the available list of topics for a particular consumer.
```ballerina
string[] result = check consumer->getAvailableTopics();
```

parameters.name: duration
parameters.description: Timeout duration (in seconds) for the execution of the `getAvailableTopics` operation

return.description:
Array of topics currently available (authorized) for the consumer to subscribe or else
a `kafka:Error`

functions.name: getBeginningOffsets
functions.description:
Retrieves the start offsets for a given set of partitions.
```ballerina
kafka:PartitionOffset[] result = check consumer->getBeginningOffsets([topicPartition1, topicPartition2]);
```

parameters.name: partitions
parameters.description: Array of topic partitions to get the starting offsets

parameters.name: duration
parameters.description: Timeout duration (in seconds) for the `getBeginningOffsets` execution

return.description: Starting offsets for the given partitions if executes successfully or else a `kafka:Error`

functions.name: getCommittedOffset
functions.description:
Retrieves the lastly committed offset for the given topic partition.
```ballerina
kafka:PartitionOffset? result = check consumer->getCommittedOffset(topicPartition);
```

parameters.name: partition
parameters.description: The `TopicPartition` in which the committed offset is returned to the consumer

parameters.name: duration
parameters.description: Timeout duration (in seconds) for the `getCommittedOffset` operation to execute

return.description:
The last committed offset for a given partition for the consumer if there is a committed offset
present, `()` if there are no committed offsets, or else a `kafka:Error`

functions.name: getEndOffsets
functions.description:
Retrieves the last offsets for a given set of partitions.
```ballerina
kafka:PartitionOffset[] result = check consumer->getEndOffsets([topicPartition1, topicPartition2]);
```

parameters.name: partitions
parameters.description: Set of partitions to get the last offsets

parameters.name: duration
parameters.description: Timeout duration (in seconds) for the `getEndOffsets` operation to execute

return.description: End offsets for the given partitions if executes successfully or else a `kafka:Error`

functions.name: getPausedPartitions
functions.description:
Retrieves the partitions, which are currently paused.
```ballerina
kafka:TopicPartition[] result = check consumer->getPausedPartitions();
```

return.description: The set of partitions paused from message retrieval if executes successfully or else a `kafka:Error`

functions.name: getPositionOffset
functions.description:
Retrieves the offset of the next record that will be fetched if a record exists in that position.
```ballerina
int result = check consumer->getPositionOffset(topicPartition);
```

parameters.name: partition
parameters.description: The `TopicPartition` in which the position is required

parameters.name: duration
parameters.description: Timeout duration (in seconds) for the get position offset operation to execute

return.description:
Offset, which will be fetched next (if a record exists in that offset) or else a `kafka:Error` if
the operation fails

functions.name: getSubscription
functions.description:
Retrieves the set of topics, which are currently subscribed by the consumer.
```ballerina
string[] result = check consumer->getSubscription();
```

return.description: Array of subscribed topics for the consumer if executes successfully or else a `kafka:Error`

functions.name: getTopicPartitions
functions.description:
Retrieves the set of partitions to which the topic belongs.
```ballerina
kafka:TopicPartition[] result = check consumer->getTopicPartitions("kafka-topic");
```

parameters.name: topic
parameters.description: The topic for which the partition information is needed

parameters.name: duration
parameters.description: Timeout duration (in seconds) for the `getTopicPartitions` operation to execute

return.description: Array of partitions for the given topic if executes successfully or else a `kafka:Error`

functions.name: pause
functions.description:
Pauses retrieving messages from a set of partitions.
```ballerina
kafka:Error? result = consumer->pause([topicPartition1, topicPartition2]);
```

parameters.name: partitions
parameters.description: Set of topic partitions to pause the retrieval of messages

return.description: A `kafka:Error` if an error is encountered or else `()`

functions.name: poll
functions.description:
Polls the external broker to retrieve messages.
```ballerina
kafka:AnydataConsumerRecord[] result = check consumer->poll(10);
```

parameters.name: timeout
parameters.description: Polling time in seconds

parameters.name: T
parameters.description: Optional type description of the required data type

return.description: Array of consumer records if executed successfully or else a `kafka:Error`

functions.name: pollPayload
functions.description:
Polls the external broker to retrieve messages in the required data type without the `kafka:AnydataConsumerRecord`
information.
```ballerina
Person[] persons = check consumer->pollPayload(10);
```

parameters.name: timeout
parameters.description: Polling time in seconds

parameters.name: T
parameters.description: Optional type description of the required data type

return.description: Array of data in the required format if executed successfully or else a `kafka:Error`

functions.name: resume
functions.description:
Resumes retrieving messages from a set of partitions, which were paused earlier.
```ballerina
kafka:Error? result = consumer->resume([topicPartition1, topicPartition2]);
```

parameters.name: partitions
parameters.description: Topic partitions to resume the retrieval of messages

return.description: A `kafka:Error` if an error is encountered or else `()`

functions.name: offsetsForTimes
functions.description:
Retrieves the offsets for the given topic partitions and timestamps.
```ballerina
kafka:TopicPartitionOffset[] result = check consumer->offsetsForTimes([[topicPartition1, timestamp1], [topicPartition2, timestamp2]]);
```

parameters.name: topicPartitionTimestamps
parameters.description: Array of topic partitions with required timestamps

parameters.name: duration
parameters.description: Timeout duration (in seconds) for the `offsetsForTimes` operation to execute

return.description: Array of topic partition offsets if executed successfully or else a `kafka:Error`

functions.name: seek
functions.description:
Seeks for a given offset in a topic partition.
```ballerina
kafka:Error? result = consumer->seek(partitionOffset);
```

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: The `PartitionOffset` to seek

return.description: A `kafka:Error` if an error is encountered or else `()`

functions.name: seekToBeginning
functions.description:
Seeks to the beginning of the offsets for a given set of topic partitions.
```ballerina
kafka:Error? result = consumer->seekToBeginning([topicPartition1, topicPartition2]);
```

parameters.name: partitions
parameters.description: The set of topic partitions to seek

return.description: A `kafka:Error` if an error is encountered or else `()`

functions.name: seekToEnd
functions.description:
Seeks to the end of the offsets for a given set of topic partitions.
```ballerina
kafka:Error? result = consumer->seekToEnd([topicPartition1, topicPartition2]);
```

parameters.name: partitions
parameters.description: The set of topic partitions to seek

return.description: A `kafka:Error` if an error is encountered or else `()`

functions.name: subscribe
functions.description:
Subscribes the consumer to the provided set of topics.
```ballerina
kafka:Error? result = consumer->subscribe(["kafka-topic-1", "kafka-topic-2"]);
```

parameters.name: topics
parameters.description: The topic/array of topics to subscribe

return.description: A `kafka:Error` if an error is encountered or else '()'

functions.name: subscribeWithPattern
functions.description:
Subscribes the consumer to the topics, which match the provided pattern.
```ballerina
kafka:Error? result = consumer->subscribeWithPattern("kafka.*");
```

parameters.name: regex
parameters.description: The pattern, which should be matched with the topics to be subscribed

return.description: A `kafka:Error` if an error is encountered or else '()'

functions.name: unsubscribe
functions.description:
Unsubscribes from all the topics that the consumer is subscribed to.

Establish an encrypted connection if the server supports encrypted connections. The connection attempt fails if
an encrypted connection cannot be established. Additionally, verifies the server Certificate Authority (CA)
certificate against the configured CA certificates. The connection attempt fails if no valid matching CA
certificates are found.

typeDefs.description:
Establish an encrypted connection if the server supports encrypted connections and verifies the server
Certificate Authority (CA) certificate against the configured CA certificates. The connection attempt fails if an
encrypted connection cannot be established or no valid matching CA certificates are found. Also, performs hostname
identity verification by checking the hostname the client uses for connecting to the server against the identity
in the certificate that the server sends to the client.

clients.name: Client
clients.description: Represents a PostgreSQL database client.

functions.name: init
functions.description: Initializes the PostgreSQL Client. The client must be kept open throughout the application lifetime.

parameters.name: host
parameters.description: Hostname of the PostgreSQL server

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: The password of the PostgreSQL server for the provided username

parameters.name: database
parameters.description:
The name of the database. The default is to connect to a database with the
same name as the username

parameters.name: port
parameters.description: Port number of the PostgreSQL server

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: The database specific PostgreSQL connection properties

parameters.name: connectionPool
parameters.description:
The `sql:ConnectionPool` object to be used within the client. If there is no
`connectionPool` provided, the global connection pool will be used

return.description: An `sql:Error` if the client creation fails

functions.name: query
functions.description:
Executes the query, which may return multiple results.
When processing the stream, make sure to consume all fetched data or close the stream.

parameters.name: sqlQuery
parameters.description: The SQL query such as `` `SELECT * from Album WHERE name=${albumName}` ``

parameters.name: rowType
parameters.description: The `typedesc` of the record to which the result needs to be returned

return.description: Stream of records in the `rowType` type

functions.name: queryRow
functions.description:
Executes the query, which is expected to return at most one row of the result.
If the query does not return any results, an `sql:NoRowsError` is returned.

parameters.name: sqlQuery
parameters.description: The SQL query such as `` `SELECT * from Album WHERE name=${albumName}` ``

parameters.name: returnType
parameters.description:
The `typedesc` of the record to which the result needs to be returned.
It can be a basic type if the query result contains only one column

return.description: Result in the `returnType` type or an `sql:Error`

functions.name: execute
functions.description: Executes the SQL query. Only the metadata of the execution is returned (not the results from the query).

parameters.name: sqlQuery
parameters.description: The SQL query such as `` `DELETE FROM Album WHERE artist=${artistName}` ``

return.description: Metadata of the query execution as an `sql:ExecutionResult` or an `sql:Error`

functions.name: batchExecute
functions.description:
Executes the SQL query with multiple sets of parameters in a batch. Only the metadata of the execution is returned (not results from the query).
If one of the commands in the batch fails, the `sql:BatchExecuteError` will be returned immediately.

parameters.name: sqlQueries
parameters.description: The SQL query with multiple sets of parameters

return.description: Metadata of the query execution as an `sql:ExecutionResult[]` or an `sql:Error`

functions.name: call
functions.description:
Executes an SQL query, which calls a stored procedure. This may or may not
return results. Once the results are processed, the `close` method on `sql:ProcedureCallResult` must be called.

parameters.name: sqlQuery
parameters.description: The SQL query such as `` `CALL sp_GetAlbums();` ``

parameters.name: rowTypes
parameters.description: `typedesc` array of the records to which the results need to be returned

return.description: Summary of the execution and results are returned in an `sql:ProcedureCallResult`, or an `sql:Error`

functions.name: close
functions.description:
Closes the PostgreSQL client and shuts down the connection pool. The client must be closed only at the end of the
application lifetime (or closed for graceful stops in a service).

clients.name: Caller
clients.description: Provides the functionality to manipulate the messages received by the consumer services.

functions.name: basicAck
functions.description:
Acknowledges one or several received messages.
```ballerina
check caller->basicAck(true);
```

parameters.name: multiple
parameters.description:
Set to `true` to acknowledge all messages up to and including the called on message and
`false` to acknowledge just the called on message

return.description: A `rabbitmq:Error` if an I/O error occurred

functions.name: basicNack
functions.description:
Rejects one or several received messages.
```ballerina
check caller->basicNack(true, requeue = false);
```

parameters.name: multiple
parameters.description:
Set to `true` to reject all messages up to and including the called on message and
`false` to reject just the called on message

parameters.name: requeue
parameters.description: `true` if the rejected message(s) should be re-queued rather than discarded/dead-lettered

return.description: A `rabbitmq:Error` if an I/O error is encountered or else `()`

clients.description: The Ballerina interface to provide AMQP Channel related functionality.

functions.name: init
functions.description:
Initializes a `rabbitmq:Client` object.
```ballerina
rabbitmq:Client rabbitmqClient = check new(rabbitmq:DEFAULT_HOST, rabbitmq:DEFAULT_PORT);
```

parameters.name: host
parameters.description: The host used for establishing the connection

parameters.name: port
parameters.description: The port used for establishing the connection

parameters.name: connectionData
parameters.description: The connection configurations

functions.name: queueDeclare
functions.description:
Declares a non-exclusive, auto-delete, and non-durable queue with the given configurations.
```ballerina
check rabbitmqClient->queueDeclare("MyQueue");
```

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name of the queue

parameters.name: config
parameters.description: The configurations required to declare a queue

return.description:
`()` if the queue was successfully generated or else a `rabbitmq:Error`
if an I/O error occurred

functions.name: queueAutoGenerate
functions.description:
Declares a queue with a server-generated name.
```ballerina
string queueName = check rabbitmqClient->queueAutoGenerate();
```

return.description:
The name of the queue or else a `rabbitmq:Error`
if an I/O error occurred

functions.name: exchangeDeclare
functions.description:
Declares a non-auto-delete, non-durable exchange with no extra arguments.
If the arguments are specified, then the exchange is declared accordingly.
```ballerina
check rabbitmqClient->exchangeDeclare("MyExchange", rabbitmq:DIRECT_EXCHANGE);
```

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name of the exchange

parameters.name: exchangeType
parameters.description: The type of the exchange

parameters.name: config
parameters.description: The configurations required to declare an exchange

return.description: A `rabbitmq:Error` if an I/O error occurred or else `()`

functions.name: queueBind
functions.description:
Binds a queue to an exchange with the given binding key.
```ballerina
check rabbitmqClient->queueBind("MyQueue", "MyExchange", "routing-key");
```

parameters.name: queueName
parameters.description: The name of the queue

parameters.name: exchangeName
parameters.description: The name of the exchange

parameters.name: bindingKey
parameters.description: The binding key used to bind the queue to the exchange

return.description: A `rabbitmq:Error` if an I/O error occurred or else `()`

functions.name: publishMessage
functions.description:
Publishes a message. Publishing to a non-existent exchange will result in a channel-level
protocol error, which closes the channel.
```ballerina
check rabbitmqClient->publishMessage(messageInBytes, "MyQueue");
```

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: The message to be published

return.description: A `rabbitmq:Error` if an I/O error occurred or else `()`

functions.name: consumeMessage
functions.description:
Retrieves a message synchronously from the given queue providing direct access to the messages in the queue.
```ballerina
rabbitmq:AnydataMessage message = check rabbitmqClient->consumeMessage("MyQueue");
```

parameters.name: queueName
parameters.description: The name of the queue

parameters.name: autoAck
parameters.description: If false, should manually acknowledge

parameters.name: T
parameters.description: Optional type description of the required data type

return.description:
A `rabbitmq:AnydataMessage` object containing the retrieved message data or else a`rabbitmq:Error` if an
I/O error occurred

functions.name: consumePayload
functions.description:
Retrieves the payload synchronously from the given queue.
```ballerina
string message = check rabbitmqClient->consumePayload("MyQueue");
```

parameters.name: queueName
parameters.description: The name of the queue

parameters.name: autoAck
parameters.description: If false, should manually acknowledge

parameters.name: T
parameters.description: Optional type description of the required data type

return.description: Message payload in the required format if executed successfully or else a `rabbitmq:Error`

functions.name: basicAck
functions.description:
Acknowledges one or several received messages.
```ballerina
check rabbitmqClient->basicAck(<message|deliveryTag>);
```

parameters.name: ackTarget
parameters.description: The message to be acknowledged or the delivery tag of the message

parameters.name: multiple
parameters.description:
Set to `true` to acknowledge all messages up to and including the called on message and
`false` to acknowledge just the called on message

return.description: A `rabbitmq:Error` if an I/O error occurred or else `()`

functions.name: basicNack
functions.description:
Rejects one or several received messages.
```ballerina
check rabbitmqClient->basicNack(<message|deliveryTag>);
```

parameters.name: ackTarget
parameters.description: The message to be rejected or the delivery tag of the message

parameters.name: multiple
parameters.description:
Set to `true` to reject all messages up to and including the called on message and
`false` to reject just the called on message

parameters.name: requeue
parameters.description: `true` if the rejected message(s) should be re-queued rather than discarded/dead-lettered

return.description: A `rabbitmq:Error` if an I/O error occurred or else `()`

functions.name: queueDelete
functions.description:
Deletes the queue with the given name although it is in use or has messages in it.
If the `ifUnused` or `ifEmpty` parameters are given, the queue is checked before deleting.
```ballerina
check rabbitmqClient->queueDelete("MyQueue");
```

parameters.name: queueName
parameters.description: The name of the queue to be deleted

parameters.name: ifUnused
parameters.description: True if the queue should be deleted only if it's not in use

parameters.name: ifEmpty
parameters.description: True if the queue should be deleted only if it's empty

return.description: A `rabbitmq:Error` if an I/O error occurred or else `()`

functions.name: exchangeDelete
functions.description:
Deletes the exchange with the given name.
```ballerina
check rabbitmqClient->exchangeDelete("MyExchange");
```

parameters.name: exchangeName
parameters.description: The name of the exchange

return.description: A `rabbitmq:Error` if an I/O error occurred or else `()`

functions.name: queuePurge
functions.description:
Purges the content of the given queue.
```ballerina
check rabbitmqClient->queuePurge("MyQueue");
```

fields.name: UserOrGroupId
fields.description: ID of the User or Group that has been given access to the Account. This field can't be updated.

fields.name: AccountAccessLevel
fields.description: Level of access that the User or Group has to the Account. The possible values are: Read Edit All (This value isn't valid for create or update calls.) This field must be set to an access level that is at least equal to the organization’s default Account access level. In addition, either this field, the OpportunityAccessLevel field, or the CaseAccessLevel field must be set higher than the organization’s default access level.

fields.name: OpportunityAccessLevel
fields.description: Level of access that the User or Group has to opportunities associated with the Account. The possible values are: None Read Edit This field must be set to an access level that is at least equal to the organization’s default opportunity access level. This field can’t be updated via the API if the AccountAccessLevel field is set to All. You can't use the API to update this field for the associated Account owner. You must update the Account owner’s opportunityAccessLevel via the Salesforce user interface.

fields.name: CaseAccessLevel
fields.description: Level of access that the User or Group has to cases associated with the account. The possible values are: None Read Edit This field must be set to an access level that is at least equal to the organization’s default CaseAccessLevel. This field can't be updated via the API if the AccountAccessLevel field is set to All. You can't update this field for the associated account owner via the API. You must update the account owner’s CaseAccessLevel via the Salesforce user interface.

fields.name: ContactAccessLevel
fields.description: Level of access that the User or Group has to contacts associated with the account. The possible values are: None Read Edit This field must be set to an access level that is at least equal to the organization’s default ContactAccessLevel. This field can't be updated via the API if the ContactAccessLevel field is set to “Controlled by Parent.” You can't update this field for the associated account owner using the API. You must update the account owner’s ContactAccessLevel via the Salesforce user interface.

fields.name: RowCause
fields.description: Reason that this sharing entry exists. You can only write to this field when its value is either omitted or set to Manual (default). You can create a value for this field in API versions 32.0 and later with the correct organization-wide sharing settings.
