fields.description: Address Single close or exact match with the address, or an address that shares the house number. Near address Single match point with a calculated possible address along the street segment of the address. Block Single close match with a street address centered on a block. Street Single close match with an address at the center of the street segment. Extended Zip Single close match with the address centered in the extended postal code. A more specific location within a ZIP code. Zip Single close match with the address centered in the postal code. Locality The center of a village, suburb, neighborhood, or another locally recognized geographic boundary where the address is located. City The center of the city where the address is located. County The largest administrative division of most states in the United States where the address is located. State A geographical and political boundary that is part of the United States where the address is located. California is a state in the United States. Unknown The address could not be found.

fields.description: The timestamp for when the current user last viewed this record. If this value is null, this record might only have been referenced (LastReferencedDate) and not viewed.

fields.name: LastReferencedDate
fields.description: The timestamp for when the current user last viewed a record related to this record.

typeDefs.name: DocumentSObject
typeDefs.description: Represents a file that a user has uploaded. Unlike Attachment records, documents are not attached to a parent object.

fields.name: DomainId
fields.description: The ID of the associated Domain.

fields.name: SiteId
fields.description: The ID of the associated Site.

fields.name: PathPrefix
fields.description: Shows where a site’s root exists on a domain. Can only be set for custom Web addresses. Always begins with a /.

typeDefs.name: DomainSiteSObject
typeDefs.description: Read-only junction object that joins together the Site and Domain objects.

fields.name: DomainType
fields.description: The global namespace that this custom Web address belongs to. This value is set to DNS for custom Web addresses in the global DNS. DomainType can have the following value: DNS—Domain Name System (DNS)

fields.name: Domain
fields.description: The branded custom Web address within the global namespace identified by this domain's type. In the Domain Name System (DNS) global namespace, this field is the custom Web address that you registered with a third-party domain name registrar. The custom Web address can be used to access the site of this domain.

fields.name: CnameTarget
fields.description: The canonical name (CNAME) of the external host or server. If you use a custom domain with a non-Salesforce provider, such as your own external server or CDN provider, to serve your domain, this field points to the CNAME of the external provider. This field is available in API version 43.0 and later.

fields.name: HttpsOption
fields.description: Current HTTPS option. Values may include: CdnPartner—Content Delivery Network (CDN) partner of Salesforce Community—Experience Cloud site Force.com Subdomain CommunityAlt—Experience Cloud site My Domain ExternalHttps—Domain is served by an external host NoHttps—No HTTPS OrgDomain—My Domain Sites—Salesforce Sites Subdomain SitesAlt—Salesforce Sites My Domain SitesRuntime—Salesforce Cloud This field is available in API version 47.0 and higher.

typeDefs.name: DomainSObject
typeDefs.description: Read-only object that represents a custom Web address assigned to a site in your organization.

fields.name: Name
fields.description: The autogenerated name that’s given to the Duplicate Record Item. Label is Duplicate Record Item Name.

fields.name: DuplicateRecordSetId
fields.description: The duplicate record set that the duplicate record item is assigned to.

fields.name: RecordId
fields.description: The name of the record as it appears on the record’s detail page.

typeDefs.name: DuplicateRecordItemSObject
typeDefs.description: Represents an individual record that’s part of a duplicate record set. Use this object to create custom report types.

fields.name: Name
fields.description: The autogenerated name that’s given to the duplicate record set. Label is Duplicate Record Set Name.

fields.name: LastViewedDate
fields.description: The timestamp when the current user last viewed this record or list view. If this value is null, the user might have only accessed this record or list view (LastReferencedDate) but not viewed it.

fields.name: LastReferencedDate
fields.description: The timestamp when the current user last accessed this record, a record related to this record, or a list view.

fields.name: DuplicateRuleId
fields.description: The duplicate rule used to identify this list of duplicate records.

fields.name: RecordCount
fields.description: The number of record items in the set.

typeDefs.name: DuplicateRecordSetSObject
typeDefs.description: Represents a group of records that have been identified as duplicates. Each duplicate record set contains one or more duplicate record items. Use this object to create custom report types and view the results of duplicate jobs.

fields.name: SobjectType
fields.description: The type of object the duplicate rule is defined for. For example, account, contact, or lead.

fields.name: DeveloperName
fields.description: The developer name for the duplicate rule.

fields.name: Language
fields.description: The language for the duplicate rule.

fields.name: MasterLabel
fields.description: The label for the duplicate rule.

fields.name: IsActive
fields.description: Indicates whether a duplicate rule is active (true) or not (false). This field is read only.

typeDefs.name: DuplicateRuleSObject
typeDefs.description: Represents a duplicate rule for detecting duplicate records.

fields.name: PriorityNumber
fields.description: Indicates the order in which the email domain filter is processed. Filters are evaluated in ascending order. The priority number must be unique. If this field is left blank, it is assigned the next available number and is processed last. Processing stops after the first matching filter is applied.

fields.name: EmailRelayId
fields.description: The ID of the EmailRelay record.

fields.name: ToDomain
fields.description: Restricts the email relay to send emails based on the recipient domains (ToDomain) listed in this field. This field is optional, accepts a list of comma-separated values, and supports the wildcard character.

fields.name: FromDomain
fields.description: Restricts the email relay to send emails based on the sender domains (FromDomain) listed in this field. This field is optional, accepts a list of comma-separated values, and supports the wildcard character.

fields.name: IsActive
fields.description: Indicates whether the email domain filter is active (true) or not (false). Use this field to enable or disable the email domain filter.

typeDefs.name: EmailDomainFilterSObject
typeDefs.description: Represents a filter that determines whether an email relay is restricted to a specific list of domains.

fields.name: Selector
fields.description: Text used to distinguish the DKIM key from any other DKIM keys your organization uses for the specified domain.

fields.name: Domain
fields.description: The organization’s domain name that the DKIM key is generated for.

fields.name: DomainMatch
fields.description: The specificity of match required on the sending domain name before signing with this DKIM key. Valid values are: DomainOnly—Sign if sending domain matches at the domain level only (example.com but not mail.example.com) SubdomainsOnly—Sign if sending domain matches at the subdomain level only (mail.example.com but not example.com) DomainAndSubdomains—Sign if sending domain matches at the domain and subdomain levels (example.com and mail.example.com)

fields.name: IsActive
fields.description: Indicates whether this DKIM key is active (true) or not (false).

fields.name: AlternateSelector
fields.description: The text used to distinguish the DKIM key from any other DKIM keys your organization uses for the specified domain. This field is available in API version 44.0 and later after activating the Critical Update.

fields.name: TxtRecordName
fields.description: Read-only. The TXT record name is used to create the CNAME record. Refer to the Usage section for more information. This field is available in API version 44.0 and later after activating the Critical Update.

fields.name: AlternateTxtRecordName
fields.description: The alternate TXT record name is used to create the CNAME record. Refer to the Usage section for more information. This field is available in API version 44.0 and later after activating the Critical Update.

fields.name: TxtRecordsPublishState
fields.description: The possible values are: Published Publishing in progress Publishing failed This field is available in API version 44.0 and later after activating the Critical Update.

fields.name: KeySize
fields.description: Indicates the RSA key size, in bits. The possible values are: 1024 2048 This field is available in API version 45.0 and later.

fields.name: PublicKey
fields.description: Part of the domain key pair that mail recipients retrieve to decrypt the DKIM header and verify your domain. Add the PublicKey value to your domain’s DNS records before you start signing with this domain key.

fields.name: AlternatePublicKey
fields.description: Read-only. Alternate public keys are used by Salesforce to auto-rotate domain keys. This field is available in API version 44.0 and later after activating the Critical Update.

typeDefs.name: EmailDomainKeySObject
typeDefs.description: Represents a domain key for an organization’s domain, used to authenticate outbound email that Salesforce sends on the organization’s behalf.

fields.name: EmailMessageId
fields.description: The ID of the EmailMessage record.

fields.name: RelationId
fields.description: The RecordId of the sender or recipient.If a record relates an email to an email address that’s not associated with an existing contact, lead, or user record in Salesforce, the value of RelationId is null.

fields.name: RelationType
fields.description: The type of relationship the contact, lead, or user has with the email message. Possible values include: ToAddress CcAddress BccAddress FromAddress OtherAddress For an Experience Cloud site user who is not the sender of the email, no BccAddress relations are returned.

fields.name: RelationAddress
fields.description: The email address of the sender or recipient.If a record relates an email to an existing contact, lead, or user record in Salesforce, the value of RelationAddress is the current value of the email address. If the value is not set, it is auto-populated from RelationId.

fields.name: RelationObjectType
fields.description: The API name of the object type of the RecordId in the RelationId field. It can be a contact, lead, or user.

typeDefs.name: EmailMessageRelationSObject
typeDefs.description: Represents the relationship between an email and contacts, leads, and users.

fields.name: ParentId
fields.description: ID of the case that’s associated with the email.

fields.name: ActivityId
fields.description: ID of the activity that is associated with the email. Usually represents an open task that is created for the case owner when a new unread email message is received. ActivityId can only be specified for emails on cases. It’s auto-created for other entities.

fields.name: TextBody
fields.description: The body of the email, in plain text format. If TextBody is not set, then it is extracted from HtmlBody.

fields.name: HtmlBody
fields.description: The body of the email in HTML format.

fields.name: Headers
fields.description: The Internet message headers of the incoming email. Used for debugging and tracing purposes. Does not apply to outgoing emails.

fields.name: Subject
fields.description: The subject line of the email.

fields.name: FromName
fields.description: The sender’s name. When using this field, specify an email address that exists in EmailMessageRelation, with a RelationType of FromAddress.

fields.name: FromAddress
fields.description: The address that originated the email. When using this field, specify an email address that exists in EmailMessageRelation, with a RelationType of FromAddress.

fields.name: ValidatedFromAddress
fields.description: A picklist value with either the sender's address, validated org-wide email addresses that originated the email, or Email-to-Case Routing Address.ValidatedFromAddress isn’t suitable for use in Group By or Sort By statements. Use FromAddressinstead.

fields.name: ToAddress
fields.description: A string array of email addresses for recipients who were sent the email message. Include only email addresses that are not associated with Contact, Lead, or User records in Salesforce. If the recipient is a contact, lead, or user, add their ID to the ToIds field instead of adding their email address to the ToAddress field. Then the email message is automatically associated with the contact, lead, or user.

fields.name: CcAddress
fields.description: A string array of email addresses for recipients who were sent a carbon copy of the email message. Include only email addresses that are not associated with Contact, Lead, or User records in Salesforce. If the recipient is a contact, lead, or user, add their ID to the CcIds field instead of adding their email address to the CcAddress field. Then the email message is automatically associated with the contact, lead, or user.

fields.name: BccAddress
fields.description: A string array of email addresses for recipients who were sent a blind carbon copy of the email message. Include only email addresses that are not associated with Contact, Lead, or User records in Salesforce. If the recipient is a contact, lead, or user, add their ID to the BccIds field instead of adding their email address to the BccAddress field. When adding their ID, the email message is automatically associated with the contact, lead, or user. For an Experience Cloud site user who is not the sender of the email, this field returns null.

fields.name: Incoming
fields.description: Indicates whether the email was received (true) or sent (false).

fields.name: HasAttachment
fields.description: Indicates whether the email was sent with an attachment (true) or not (false).

fields.name: Status
fields.description: The status of the email. The Status field is mostly read-only. You can change the status only from New to Read.Possible values are: 0 (New) 1 (Read) 2 (Replied) 3 (Sent) 4 (Forwarded) 5 (Draft)

fields.name: MessageDate
fields.description: The date the email was created.

fields.name: IsDeleted
fields.description: Indicates whether the object has been moved to the Recycle Bin (true) or not (false). Label is Deleted.

fields.name: ReplyToEmailMessageId
fields.description: ID of the inbound or outbound email message the current email message is a reply to. It’s not possible to reply to a message whose Status is Draft.

fields.name: IsExternallyVisible
fields.description: If the Experience Cloud site case feed is enabled, IsExternallyVisible controls the external visibility of emails in sites. When IsExternallyVisible is set to true—its default value—email messages are visible to external users in the case feed.

fields.name: MessageIdentifier
fields.description: The ID of the email message.

fields.name: ThreadIdentifier
fields.description: The ID of the email thread the email message belongs to.

fields.name: IsClientManaged
fields.description: If EmailMessage is created with IsClientManaged set to true, users can modify EmailMessage.ContentDocumentIds to link file attachments even when the Status of the EmailMessage is not set to Draft.

fields.name: RelatedToId
fields.description: The RelatedToId represents nonhuman objects such as accounts, opportunities, campaigns, cases, or custom objects. RelatedToIds are polymorphic. Polymorphic means a RelatedToId is equivalent to the ID of a related object.

fields.name: IsTracked
fields.description: Indicates whether the email is being tracked.

fields.name: IsOpened
fields.description: Indicates whether the email has been opened.

fields.name: FirstOpenedDate
fields.description: The date the email was first opened.

fields.name: LastOpenedDate
fields.description: The date the email was last opened.

fields.name: IsBounced
fields.description: Indicates whether the email bounced.

fields.name: EmailTemplateId
fields.description: The email template, if any, that was chosen for the email. This field is populated in Lightning Experience only.

typeDefs.name: EmailMessageSObject
typeDefs.description: Represents an email in Salesforce.

fields.name: Host
fields.description: Indicates the host name or IP address of your company's SMTP server.

fields.name: Port
fields.description: Indicates the port number of your company's SMTP server. 25 587 10025 11025

fields.name: TlsSetting
fields.description: Specifies whether Salesforce uses TLS for SMTP sessions. Off: TLS is turned off. SMTP session continues through an insecure connection. Preferred: If the remote server supports TLS, Salesforce upgrades the current SMTP session to use TLS. If TLS is unavailable, Salesforce continues the session without TLS. Required: Salesforce continues the session only if the remote server supports TLS. If TLS is unavailable, Salesforce terminates the session without delivering the email. PreferredVerify: If the remote server supports TLS, Salesforce upgrades the current SMTP session to use TLS. Before the session begins, Salesforce verifies that the certificate is signed by a valid certificate authority, and that the common name presented in the certificate matches the domain or mail exchange of the current connection. If TLS is available but the certificate is not signed or the common name does not match, Salesforce disconnects the session and does not deliver the email. If TLS is unavailable, Salesforce continues the session without TLS. RequiredVerify: Salesforce continues the session only if the remote server supports TLS, the certificate is signed by a valid certificate authority, and the common name presented in the certificate matches the domain or mail exchange to which Salesforce is connected. If any of these criteria are not met, Salesforce terminates the session without delivering the email.

fields.name: IsRequireAuth
fields.description: Indicates whether (true) or not (false) authentication is required. When setting this field to true, the TlsSetting must be set to RequiredVerify. This field is available in API version 44.0 and later.

fields.name: Username
fields.description: Specifies the username for relay host STMP authentication. When IsRequireAuth is set to true, this field is required. This field is available in API version 44.0 and later.

fields.name: Password
fields.description: Specifies the password for relay host STMP authentication. When IsRequireAuth is set to true, this field is required. This field is available in API version 44.0 and later.

typeDefs.name: EmailRelaySObject
typeDefs.description: Represents the configuration for sending an email relay. An email relay routes email sent from Salesforce through your company’s email servers.

fields.name: IsActive
fields.description: Indicates whether this object is active (true) or not (false).

fields.name: LocalPart
fields.description: The local-part of the email service address. The local-part of the address is the string that comes before the @ symbol.

fields.name: EmailDomainName
fields.description: A read only field you can query that contains the system-generated domain part of this email service address. The system generates a unique domain-part for each email service address to ensure that no two email service addresses are identical.

fields.name: AuthorizedSenders
fields.description: Configures the email service address to only accept messages from the email addresses or domains listed in this field. If the email service address receives a message from an unlisted email address or domain, the email service performs the action specified in the AuthorizationFailureAction field of its associated email service. Leave this field blank if you want the email service address to receive email from any email address.

fields.name: RunAsUserId
fields.description: The username of the user whose permissions the email service assumes when processing messages sent to this address.

fields.name: FunctionId
fields.description: The ID of the email service for which the email service address receives messages.

fields.name: DeveloperName
fields.description: The name of the object in the API. This name can contain only underscores and alphanumeric characters and must be unique in your org. It must begin with a letter, not include spaces, not end with an underscore, and not contain two consecutive underscores. This 25-character field must be unique among other EmailServicesAddress records under the same EmailServiceFunction parent. In managed packages, this field prevents naming conflicts on package installations. This field is automatically generated, but you can supply your own value if you create the record using the API. With this field, a developer can change the object’s name in a managed package and the changes are reflected in a subscriber’s organization.When creating large sets of data, always specify a unique DeveloperName for each record. If no DeveloperName is specified, performance might be slow while Salesforce generates one for each record.

typeDefs.name: EmailServicesAddressSObject
typeDefs.description: An email service address.

fields.name: IsActive
fields.description: Indicates whether this object is active (true) or not (false).

fields.name: FunctionName
fields.description: The name of the email service.

fields.name: AuthorizedSenders
fields.description: Configures the email service to only accept messages from the email addresses or domains listed in this field. If the email service receives a message from an unlisted email address or domain, the email service performs the action specified in the AuthorizationFailureAction field. Leave this field blank if you want the email service to receive email from any email address.

fields.name: IsAuthenticationRequired
fields.description: Configures the email service to verify the legitimacy of the sending server before processing a message. The email service uses the SPF, SenderId, and DomainKeys protocols to verify the sender's legitimacy: If the sending server passes at least one of these protocols and does not fail any, the email service accepts the email. If the server fails a protocol or does not support any of the protocols, the email service performs the action specified in the AuthenticationFailureAction field.

fields.name: IsTlsRequired
fields.description: Not currently in use.

fields.name: AttachmentOption
fields.description: Indicates the types of attachments the email service accepts. One of the following values: None—The email service accepts the message but discards any attachment. (In API version 41.0 and earlier, the value specified for this choice is 0.) NoContent—The attachment metadata (filename, MIME type, and so on) is provided to the Apex class, but the body is set to null. There was no previous numeric value for this choice. TextOnly—The email service only accepts the following types of attachments: Attachments with a Multipurpose Internet Mail Extension (MIME) type of text. Attachments with a MIME type of application/octet-stream and a file name that ends with either a .vcf or .vcs extension. These are saved as text/x-vcard and text/calendar MIME types, respectively. (In API version 41.0 and earlier, the value specified for this choice is 1.) BinaryOnly—The email service only accepts binary attachments, such as image, audio, application, and video files. (In API version 41.0 and earlier, the value specified for this choice is 2.) All—The email service accepts any type of attachment. (In API version 41.0 and earlier, the value specified for this choice is 3.)

fields.name: ApexClassId
fields.description: Required. The ID of the Apex class that the email service uses to process inbound messages. This field is required for API version 12.0 and later.

fields.name: OverLimitAction
fields.description: Indicates what the email service does with messages if the total number of messages processed by all email services combined has reached the daily limit for your organization. One of the following values: UseSystemDefault—The system default is used. (In API version 41.0 and earlier, the value specified for this choice is 0.) Bounce—The email service returns the message to the sender with a notification that explains why the message was rejected. (In API version 41.0 and earlier, the value specified for this choice is 1.) Discard—The email service deletes the message without notifying the sender. (In API version 41.0 and earlier, the value specified for this choice is 2.) Requeue—The email service queues the message for processing in the next 24 hours. If the message is not processed within 24 hours, the email service returns the message to the sender with a notification that explains why the message was rejected. (In API version 41.0 and earlier, the value specified for this choice is 3.) The system calculates the limit by multiplying the number of user licenses by 1,000.

fields.name: FunctionInactiveAction
fields.description: Indicates what the email service does with messages it receives when the email service itself is inactive. One of the following values: UseSystemDefault—The system default is used. (In API version 41.0 and earlier, the value specified for this choice is 0.) Bounce—The email service returns the message to the sender with a notification that explains why the message was rejected. (In API version 41.0 and earlier, the value specified for this choice is 1.) Discard—The email service deletes the message without notifying the sender. (In API version 41.0 and earlier, the value specified for this choice is 2.) Requeue—The email service queues the message for processing in the next 24 hours. If the message is not processed within 24 hours, the email service returns the message to the sender with a notification that explains why the message was rejected. (In API version 41.0 and earlier, the value specified for this choice is 3.)

fields.name: AddressInactiveAction
fields.description: Indicates what the email service does with messages received at an email address that is inactive.One of the following values: UseSystemDefault—The system default is used. (In API version 41.0 and earlier, the value specified for this choice is 0.) Bounce—The email service returns the message to the sender with a notification that explains why the message was rejected. (In API version 41.0 and earlier, the value specified for this choice is 1.) Discard—The email service deletes the message without notifying the sender. (In API version 41.0 and earlier, the value specified for this choice is 2.) Requeue—The email service queues the message for processing in the next 24 hours. If the message is not processed within 24 hours, the email service returns the message to the sender with a notification that explains why the message was rejected. (In API version 41.0 and earlier, the value specified for this choice is 3.)

fields.name: AuthenticationFailureAction
fields.description: Indicates what the email service does with messages that fail or do not support any of the authentication protocols if the IsAuthenticationRequired field is true. One of the following values: UseSystemDefault—The system default is used. (In API version 41.0 and earlier, the value specified for this choice is 0.) Bounce—The email service returns the message to the sender with a notification that explains why the message was rejected. (In API version 41.0 and earlier, the value specified for this choice is 1.) Discard—The email service deletes the message without notifying the sender. (In API version 41.0 and earlier, the value specified for this choice is 2.) Requeue—The email service queues the message for processing in the next 24 hours. If the message is not processed within 24 hours, the email service returns the message to the sender with a notification that explains why the message was rejected. (In API version 41.0 and earlier, the value specified for this choice is 3.)

fields.name: AuthorizationFailureAction
fields.description: Indicates what the email service does with messages received from senders who are not listed in the AuthorizedSenders field on either the email service or email service address.One of the following values: UseSystemDefault—The system default is used. (In API version 41.0 and earlier, the value specified for this choice is 0.) Bounce—The email service returns the message to the sender with a notification that explains why the message was rejected. (In API version 41.0 and earlier, the value specified for this choice is 1.) Discard—The email service deletes the message without notifying the sender. (In API version 41.0 and earlier, the value specified for this choice is 2.) Requeue—The email service queues the message for processing in the next 24 hours. If the message is not processed within 24 hours, the email service returns the message to the sender with a notification that explains why the message was rejected. (In API version 41.0 and earlier, the value specified for this choice is 3.)

fields.name: IsErrorRoutingEnabled
fields.description: When incoming email messages can’t be processed, indicates whether error notification email messages are routed to a chosen address or to the senders.

fields.name: ErrorRoutingAddress
fields.description: The destination email address for error notification email messages when IsErrorRoutingEnabled is true.

fields.name: IsTextAttachmentsAsBinary
fields.description: If true, text attachments are supplied to the Apex code as a Messaging.BinaryAttachment instead of as a Messaging.TextAttachment. This means that the body is supplied as an Apex Blob instead of as an Apex String.

typeDefs.name: EmailServicesFunctionSObject
typeDefs.description: An email service.

fields.name: TaskId
fields.description: The activity (task or event) associated with the email. Label is Activity ID.

fields.name: WhoId
fields.description: The WhoId represents a human such as a lead or a contact. WhoIds are polymorphic. Polymorphic means a WhoId is equivalent to a contact’s ID or a lead’s ID. The label is Name ID.

fields.name: TimesOpened
fields.description: Number of times the recipient opened the email.

fields.name: FirstOpenDate

fields.name: LastOpenDate

fields.name: EmailTemplateName

typeDefs.name: EmailStatusSObject

fields.name: Name

fields.name: DeveloperName
fields.description: The unique name of the object in the API. This name can contain only underscores and alphanumeric characters, and must be unique in your org. It must begin with a letter, not include spaces, not end with an underscore, and not contain two consecutive underscores. In managed packages, this field prevents naming conflicts on package installations. With this field, a developer can change the object’s name in a managed package and the changes are reflected in a subscriber’s organization. Label is Template Unique Name.When creating large sets of data, always specify a unique DeveloperName for each record. If no DeveloperName is specified, performance may slow while Salesforce generates one for each record.

fields.name: OwnerId
fields.description: ID of the owner of the template.

fields.name: FolderId
fields.description: ID of the folder that contains the template.

fields.name: FolderName
fields.description: The name of the folder that contains the template.

fields.name: BrandTemplateId
fields.description: Required. ID of the BrandTemplate associated with this email template. The brand template supplies letterhead information for the email template.

fields.name: EnhancedLetterheadId
fields.description: ID of the enhanced letterhead associated with the email template.To use an enhanced letterhead, associate it with a Lightning email template that uses the HML merge language.

fields.name: TemplateStyle
fields.description: Style of the template.

fields.name: IsActive
fields.description: Indicates that this template is active if true, or inactive if false.

fields.name: TemplateType
fields.description: Type of template.

fields.name: Encoding
fields.description: Character set encoding for the template.

fields.name: Description
fields.description: Description of the template, for example, Promotion Mass Mailing.

fields.name: Subject
fields.description: Content of the subject line.

fields.name: HtmlValue
fields.description: This field contains the content of the email message, including HTML coding to render the email message. Limit: 384 KB.

fields.name: Body
fields.description: Content of the email. Limit: 384 KB.

fields.name: TimesUsed
fields.description: Number of times this template has been used.

fields.name: LastUsedDate
fields.description: Date and time when this EmailTemplate was last used.

fields.name: ApiVersion
fields.description: The API version for this class. Every class has an API version specified at creation.

fields.name: Markup
fields.description: The Visualforce markup, HTML, JavaScript, or any other Web-enabled code that defines the content of the template.

fields.name: RelatedEntityType
fields.description: When UIType is 2 (Lightning Experience) or 3 (Lightning ExperienceSample), RelatedEntityType indicates which entities this template can be used with. Valid values are the entity API name: "Account" for account, "Contact" for contact, "Opportunity" for opportunity, "Lead" for lead, and so on. The value can be any entity the user has read access to (including custom entities) but not virtual entities, setup entities, or platform entities.

fields.name: IsBuilderContent
fields.description: If the email template was made in Email Template Builder. The default value is false.

typeDefs.name: EmailTemplateSObject

fields.name: DurableId

fields.name: Site

fields.name: PrimaryColor
fields.description: Value of the PrimaryColor field in the EmbeddedServiceBranding setup object.

fields.name: SecondaryColor

fields.name: ContrastPrimaryColor

fields.name: ContrastInvertedColor
fields.description: Accent branding color used in the embedded component, displayed as a hexadecimal value. Changes made to this field in the API aren’t reflected in the embedded component.

fields.name: NavBarColor

fields.name: NavBarTextColor

fields.name: SecondaryNavBarColor

fields.name: Font

fields.name: IsLiveAgentEnabled
fields.description: Specifies whether Chat is enabled for this Embedded Service deployment (true) or not (false).

fields.name: IsFieldServiceEnabled
fields.description: Specifies whether Field Service is enabled for this Embedded Service deployment (true) or not (false). Embedded Appointment Management is currently beta.

fields.name: Width
fields.description: Width of the embedded component.

fields.name: Height
fields.description: Height of the embedded component.

fields.name: IsPrechatEnabled

fields.name: CustomPrechatComponent

fields.name: FontSize

fields.name: OfflineCaseBackgroundImg

fields.name: IsQueuePositionEnabled

fields.name: ShouldShowNewAppointment

fields.name: ShouldShowExistingAppointment

fields.name: FieldServiceHomeImg
fields.description: URL of the image used for the home screen in embedded Appointment Management (beta).

fields.name: FieldServiceLogoImg
fields.description: URL of the logo used for the home screen in embedded Appointment Management (beta).

fields.name: FieldServiceConfirmCardImg
fields.description: URL of the image used for the confirmation card in embedded Appointment Management (beta).

fields.name: ShouldHideAuthDialog
fields.description: Specifies whether the prompt that the customer log in again during a flow should be hidden (true) or not (false). When it’s hidden, the customer is taken directly to your login page.

fields.name: CustomMinimizedComponent
fields.description: The custom Aura component that’s used for the minimized state for this Embedded Chat deployment.

typeDefs.name: EmbeddedServiceDetailSObject
typeDefs.description: Represents a metadata catalog object that exposes fields from the underlying Embedded Service setup objects defined in each EmbeddedServiceConfig deployment for guest users. Guest users don’t have direct access to the Embedded Service setup objects.

fields.name: DurableId
fields.description: The unique name containing EmbeddedServiceConfig.labelKey.

fields.name: EmbeddedServiceConfigDeveloperName
fields.description: Developer name for the EmbeddedServiceConfig.

fields.name: LabelKey
fields.description: The type of label for this embedded component. The value corresponds to the label within a label group (substate of chat state or page type).

fields.name: CustomLabelName

typeDefs.name: EmbeddedServiceLabelSObject
typeDefs.description: Represents a customized label in Embedded Chat or embedded Appointment Management.

fields.name: OwnerId

fields.name: Name

fields.name: LastViewedDate
fields.description: The timestamp for when the current user last viewed this record. If this value is null, it’s possible that this record was referenced (LastReferencedDate) and not viewed.

fields.name: LastReferencedDate
fields.description: The timestamp for when the current user last viewed a record related to this record.

fields.name: ContactPointType
fields.description: The contact point type of the channel.

typeDefs.name: EngagementChannelTypeSObject
typeDefs.description: Represents a channel through which a customer can be reached for communication.

fields.name: Name
fields.description: The name of the enhanced letterhead, such as Standard Company Letterhead.

fields.name: LastViewedDate
fields.description: Date and time when this enhanced letterhead was last viewed.

fields.name: LastReferencedDate

fields.name: Description
fields.description: Description of the contents of the header and footer.

fields.name: LetterheadHeader
fields.description: The contents of the enhanced letterhead’s header.

fields.name: LetterheadFooter
fields.description: The contents of the enhanced letterhead’s footer.

typeDefs.name: EnhancedLetterheadSObject
typeDefs.description: Represents an enhanced letterhead that can be associated with a Lightning email template that doesn’t use the Salesforce Merge Language (SML).

fields.name: IsDeleted
fields.description: Indicates whether the object has been moved to the Recycle Bin (true) or not (false). Label is Deleted.

fields.name: Name

fields.name: EntitlementId
fields.description: Required. ID of the Entitlement associated with the entitlement contact. Must be a valid ID.

fields.name: ContactId

typeDefs.name: EntitlementContactSObject
typeDefs.description: Represents a Contact eligible to receive customer support via an Entitlement.

fields.name: Name
fields.description: Required. Name of the entitlement.

fields.name: LastViewedDate
fields.description: The timestamp when the current user last viewed this record or list view. If this value is null, the user might have only accessed this record or list view (LastReferencedDate) but not viewed it.

fields.name: LastReferencedDate
fields.description: The timestamp when the current user last accessed this record, a record related to this record, or a list view.

fields.name: AccountId
fields.description: ID of the Account associated with the entitlement.

fields.name: Type
fields.description: The type of entitlement, such as Web or phone support.

fields.name: ServiceContractId
fields.description: Required. ID of the ServiceContract associated with the entitlement. Must be a valid ID.

fields.name: ContractLineItemId
fields.description: Required. ID of the ContractLineItem associated with the entitlement. Must be a valid ID.

fields.name: AssetId
fields.description: Required. ID of the Asset associated with the entitlement. Must be a valid asset ID.

fields.name: StartDate
fields.description: The first date the entitlement is in effect.

fields.name: EndDate
fields.description: The last day the entitlement is in effect.

fields.name: SlaProcessId
fields.description: ID of the SlaProcess associated with the entitlement. This field is available in version 19.0 and later.

fields.name: BusinessHoursId
fields.description: Required. ID of the BusinessHours associated with the entitlement. Must be a valid business hours ID.

fields.name: IsPerIncident
fields.description: Indicates whether the entitlement is limited to supporting a specific number of cases (true) or not (false).

fields.name: CasesPerEntitlement

fields.name: RemainingCases

fields.name: Status
fields.description: Status of the entitlement, such as Expired.

fields.name: SvcApptBookingWindowsId
fields.description: The operating hours that the entitlement’s work orders should respect. The label in the user interface is Operating Hours. Available only if Field Service is enabled.

fields.name: WorkOrdersPerEntitlement
fields.description: Total number of work orders available for this entitlement.

fields.name: RemainingWorkOrders
fields.description: The number of agreed work orders remaining to be created.

typeDefs.name: EntitlementSObject
typeDefs.description: Represents the customer support an account or contact is eligible to receive.

fields.name: Name
fields.description: Required. Name of the entitlement template.

fields.name: BusinessHoursId
fields.description: ID of the BusinessHours associated with the entitlement template. Must be a valid business hours ID.

fields.name: Type
fields.description: The type of entitlement template, such as Web or phone support.

fields.name: SlaProcessId
fields.description: ID of the SlaProcess associated with the entitlement template. This field is available in API version 19.0 and later.

fields.name: IsPerIncident
fields.description: Indicates whether the entitlement template is limited to supporting a specific number of cases (true) or not (false).

fields.name: CasesPerEntitlement
fields.description: The total number of cases the entitlement template supports.

fields.name: Term
fields.description: Number of days that the entitlement template is valid.

typeDefs.name: EntitlementTemplateSObject
typeDefs.description: Represents predefined terms of customer support for a product (Product2).

fields.name: Name
fields.description: The name of the milestone.

fields.name: ParentEntityId
fields.description: The ID of the record—for example, a work order—that contains the milestone.

fields.name: StartDate
fields.description: The date and time that milestone tracking started.

fields.name: TargetDate
fields.description: The date and time to complete the milestone.

fields.name: CompletionDate
fields.description: The date and time the milestone was completed.

fields.name: SlaProcessId
fields.description: The entitlement process associated with the milestone.

fields.name: MilestoneTypeId
fields.description: The ID of the milestone (for instance, First Response).

fields.name: IsCompleted
fields.description: Icon () that indicates a milestone completion.

fields.name: IsViolated
fields.description: Icon () that indicates a milestone violation.

fields.name: TargetResponseInMins
fields.description: The number of minutes to complete the milestone. Automatically calculated to include the business hours on the record.

fields.name: TargetResponseInHrs
fields.description: The number of hours to complete the milestone. Automatically calculated to include the business hours on the record.

fields.name: TargetResponseInDays
fields.description: The number of days to complete the milestone. Automatically calculated to include the business hours on the record.

fields.name: TimeRemainingInMins
fields.description: The minutes that remain before a milestone violation. Automatically calculated to include the business hours on the record.

fields.name: TimeRemainingInHrs
fields.description: The hours that remain before a milestone violation. Automatically calculated to include the business hours on the record.

fields.name: TimeRemainingInDays
fields.description: The days that remain before a milestone violation. Automatically calculated to include the business hours on the record.

fields.name: ElapsedTimeInMins
fields.description: The number of minutes it took to complete a milestone, including time during which the milestone was stopped. Automatically calculated to include the business hours on the record. Elapsed time is calculated only after the Completion Date field is populated. (Elapsed Time) – (Stopped Time) = (Actual Elapsed Time).

fields.name: ElapsedTimeInHrs
fields.description: The number of hours it took to complete a milestone, including time during which the milestone was stopped. Automatically calculated to include the business hours on the record. Elapsed time is calculated only after the Completion Date field is populated. (Elapsed Time) – (Stopped Time) = (Actual Elapsed Time).

fields.name: ElapsedTimeInDays
fields.description: The number of days it took to complete a milestone, including time during which the milestone was stopped. Automatically calculated to include the business hours on the record. Elapsed time is calculated only after the Completion Date field is populated. (Elapsed Time) – (Stopped Time) = (Actual Elapsed Time).

fields.name: TimeSinceTargetInMins
fields.description: The minutes that have elapsed since a milestone violation. Automatically calculated to include the business hours on the record.

fields.name: TimeSinceTargetInHrs
fields.description: The hours that have elapsed since a milestone violation. Automatically calculated to include the business hours on the record.

fields.name: TimeSinceTargetInDays
fields.description: The days that have elapsed since a milestone violation. Automatically calculated to include the business hours on the record.

fields.name: BusinessHoursId
fields.description: The business hours on the milestone. If business hours aren’t specified, the entitlement process business hours are used. If business hours are also not specified on the entitlement process, the business hours on the record are used.

typeDefs.name: EntityMilestoneSObject
typeDefs.description: Represents a required step in a customer support process on a work order. The Salesforce user interface uses the term “object milestone.”

fields.name: ParentId
fields.description: Required. ID of the record or user which the user is following.

fields.name: SubscriberId
fields.description: Required. ID of the user who is following the record or user.

typeDefs.name: EntitySubscriptionSObject
typeDefs.description: Represents a subscription for a user following a record or another user.

fields.name: ExternalId
fields.description: The ID of the subscriber. For example, the trigger ID.

fields.name: Name
fields.description: The name of the subscribed item, such as the trigger or process name. If the subscribed item’s name is “Process”, at least one flow Pause element is subscribed to the event.

fields.name: Type
fields.description: The subscriber type (ApexTrigger). If the subscriber is a process or flow Pause element, the type is blank.

fields.name: Topic
fields.description: The name of the subscription channel that corresponds to a platform event or change event. For a platform event, the topic name is the event name appended with __e, such as MyEvent__e. For a change event, the topic is the name of the change event, such as AccountChangeEvent.

fields.name: Position
fields.description: The replay ID of the last event that the subscriber processed.

fields.name: Tip
fields.description: The replay ID of the last published event.For high-volume platform events and change events, the value for Tip isn’t available and is always -1.

fields.name: Retries
fields.description: The number of times the trigger was retried due to throwing the EventBus.RetryableException. This field applies to Apex triggers only. Available in API version 43.0 and later.

fields.name: LastError
fields.description: The error message that the last thrown EventBus.RetryableException contains. This field applies to Apex triggers only. Available in API version 43.0 and later.

fields.name: Status
fields.description: Indicates the status of the subscriber. Can be one of the following values: Running—The subscriber is actively listening to events. If you modify the subscriber, the subscription continues to process events. Error— The subscriber was disconnected and stopped receiving published events. A trigger reaches this state when it exceeds the number of maximum retries with the EventBus.RetryableException. Trigger assertion failures and unhandled exceptions don’t cause the error state. We recommend limiting the retries to fewer than nine times to avoid reaching this state. When you fix and save the trigger, or for a managed package trigger, if you redeploy the package, the trigger resumes automatically from the tip, starting from new events. Also, you can resume a trigger subscription in the subscription detail page that you access from the platform event page. Suspended—The subscriber is disconnected and can’t receive events because a Salesforce admin suspended it or due to an internal error. You can resume a trigger subscription in the subscription detail page that you access from the platform event page. To resume a process, deactivate it and then reactivate it. If you modify the subscriber, the subscription resumes automatically from the tip, starting from new events.

typeDefs.name: EventBusSubscriberSObject
typeDefs.description: Represents a trigger, process, or flow that’s subscribed to a platform event or a change data capture event. Doesn’t include CometD subscribers.

fields.name: EventType
fields.description: The event type—API, Login, Report, URI, and so forth. Use to determine which files were generated for your org. For the corresponding LogFile schema, see EventLogFile Supported Event Types.

fields.name: LogDate
fields.description: The date and time of the log file’s creation. For daily event log files, tracks usage activity for a 24-hour period, from 12:00 a.m. to 11:59 p.m. UTC time. For hourly event log files, indicates the hour in which the log file was generated. For example, for events that occur between 11:00 AM and 12:00 PM on 3/7/2016, this field’s value is 2016-03-07T11:00:00.000Z.For hourly event log files, we recommend using CreatedDate to query the date and time that an EventLogFile object was created.

fields.name: LogFileLength
fields.description: The log file length in bytes. You can use this field to plan storage needs for your log files.

fields.name: LogFileContentType
fields.description: The content type of the log file; always .csv.

fields.name: ApiVersion
fields.description: The specific API version for this log file. This field is available in API version 30.0 and later.

fields.name: Sequence
fields.description: The number for the portion of the event log file data captured in an hour. For 24-hour event log file generation, the value of this field is 0. For hourly event log files, the initial value is 1. This value increases by 1 when events are added in the same hour after the latest event log file is created. The value resets to 1 in the subsequent hour. For example, you have activity between 2:00 and 3:00 PM. Two-log files are generated that contain the event log data for that hour, with Sequence values of 1 and 2. For event log data that occurs at 3:01 PM, the Sequence value resets to 1. This field is available in API version 37.0 and later.

fields.name: Interval
fields.description: The generation schedule for the event log file. Possible values are: Daily Hourly This field is available in API version 37.0 and later.

fields.name: LogFileFieldNames
fields.description: The ordered list of fields in the log file data. LogFileFieldNames and LogFileFieldTypes are specific to each EventType. For example, LogFileFieldNames has a different value for an API EventType and a Login EventType.

fields.name: LogFileFieldTypes
fields.description: The ordered list of field types in the log file data (String, Id, and so forth). LogFileFieldNames and LogFileFieldTypes are specific to each EventType. For example, LogFileFieldTypes has a different value for an API EventType and a Login EventType.

fields.name: LogFile
fields.description: Encoded file data in .csv format. The EventType field defines the schema for this data.

typeDefs.name: EventLogFileSObject
typeDefs.description: Represents event log files for event monitoring. The event monitoring product gathers information about your Salesforce org’s operational events, which you can use to analyze usage trends and user behavior.

fields.name: RelationId
fields.description: Contains the ID of the person (User, Contact, or Lead) or the resource invited to an event. When Shared Activities is enabled, RelationId can also contain the ID of an account, opportunity, or other object related to an event.

fields.name: EventId
fields.description: Contains the ID of the event. This value can’t be changed after it’s been specified.

fields.name: Status
fields.description: Indicates the invitee status with one of the following values: New: Invitee has received the invitation but hasn’t yet responded. This value is the default. Declined: Invitee has declined the invitation. Accepted: Invitee has accepted the invitation. Uninvited and Maybe aren’t currently supported.

fields.name: RespondedDate
fields.description: Indicates the most recent date and time when the invitee responded to an invitation to an event.

fields.name: Response
fields.description: Contains optional text that the invitee can enter when responding to an invitation to an event.

fields.name: IsDeleted
fields.description: Indicates whether the object has been moved to the Recycle Bin (true) or not (false). Label is Deleted.

typeDefs.name: EventRelationSObject
typeDefs.description: Represents a person (a user, lead, or contact) or a resource (such as a conference room) invited to an event. This object lets you add or remove invitees from an event and use the API to manage invitees’ responses to invitations. If Shared Activities is enabled, EventRelation can also represent other objects that are related to an event. EventRelation does not support triggers, workflow, or data validation rules.

fields.name: WhoId
fields.description: The WhoId represents a human such as a lead or a contact. WhoIds are polymorphic. Polymorphic means a WhoId is equivalent to a contact’s ID or a lead’s ID. The label is Name ID. If Shared Activities is enabled, the value of this field is the ID of the related lead or primary contact. If you add, update, or remove the WhoId field, you might encounter problems with triggers, workflows, and data validation rules that are associated with the record. The label is Name ID. If the JunctionIdList field is used, all WhoIds are included in the relationship list. Beginning in API version 37.0, if the contact or lead ID in the WhoId field is not in the EventWhoIds list, no error occurs and the ID is added to the EventWhoIds as the primary WhoId. If WhoId is set to null, an arbitrary ID from the existing EventWhoIds list is promoted to the primary position.

fields.name: WhatId
fields.description: The WhatId represents nonhuman objects such as accounts, opportunities, campaigns, cases, or custom objects. WhatIds are polymorphic. Polymorphic means a WhatId is equivalent to the ID of a related object. The label is Related To ID.

fields.name: Subject
fields.description: The subject line of the event, such as Call, Email, or Meeting. Limit: 255 characters.

fields.name: Location
fields.description: Contains the location of the event.

fields.name: IsAllDayEvent
fields.description: Indicates whether the ActivityDate field (true) or the ActivityDateTime field (false) is used to define the date or time of the event. Label is All-Day Event. See also DurationInMinutes and EndDateTime.

fields.name: ActivityDateTime
fields.description: Contains the event’s due date if the IsAllDayEvent flag is set to false. The time portion of this field is always transferred in the Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) time zone. Translate the time portion to or from a local time zone for the user or the application, as appropriate. Label is Due Date Time. This field is required in versions 12.0 and earlier if the IsAllDayEvent flag is set to false. The value for this field and StartDateTime must match, or one of them must be null.

fields.name: ActivityDate
fields.description: Contains the event’s due date if the IsAllDayEvent flag is set to true. This field is a date field with a timestamp that is always set to midnight in the Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) time zone. Don’t attempt to alter the timestamp to account for time zone differences. Label is Due Date Only. This field is required in versions 12.0 and earlier if the IsAllDayEvent flag is set to true. The value for this field and StartDateTime must match, or one of them must be null.

fields.name: DurationInMinutes
fields.description: Contains the event length, in minutes. Even though this field represents a temporal value, it is an integer type—not a Date/Time type. Required in versions 12.0 and earlier if IsAllDayEvent is false. In versions 13.0 and later, this field is optional, depending on the following: If IsAllDayEvent is true, you can supply a value for either DurationInMinutes or EndDateTime. Supplying values in both fields is allowed if the values add up to the same amount of time. If both fields are null, the duration defaults to one day. If IsAllDayEvent is false, a value must be supplied for either DurationInMinutes or EndDateTime. Supplying values in both fields is allowed if the values add up to the same amount of time. If the multiday event feature is enabled, then API versions 13.0 and later support values greater than 1440 for the DurationInMinutes field. API versions 12.0 and earlier can’t access event objects whose DurationInMinutes is greater than 1440. For more information, see Multiday Events. Depending on your API version, errors with the DurationInMinutes and EndDateTime fields may appear in different places. Versions 38.0 and before—Errors always appear in the DurationInMinutes field. Versions 39.0 and later—If there’s no value for the DurationInMinutes field, errors appear in the EndDateTime field. Otherwise, they appear in the DurationInMinutes field.

fields.name: StartDateTime
fields.description: Indicates the start date and time of the event. Available in versions 13.0 and later. If the Event IsAllDayEvent flag is set to true (indicating that it is an all-day Event), then the event start date information is contained in the StartDateTime field. The time portion of this field is always transferred in the Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) time zone. Translate the time portion to or from a local time zone for the user or the application, as appropriate. If the Event IsAllDayEvent flag is set to false (indicating that it is not an all-day event), then the event start date information is contained in the StartDateTime field. The time portion is always transferred in the Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) time zone. You need to translate the time portion to or from a local time zone for the user or the application, as appropriate. If this field has a value, then ActivityDate and ActivityDateTime must either be null or match the value of this field.

fields.name: EndDateTime
fields.description: Available in versions 13.0 and later. The time portion of this field is always transferred in the Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) time zone. Translate the time portion to or from a local time zone for the user or the application, as appropriate. This field is optional, depending on the following: If IsAllDayEvent is true, you can supply a value for either DurationInMinutes or EndDateTime. Supplying values in both fields is allowed if the values add up to the same amount of time. If both fields are null, the duration defaults to one day. If IsAllDayEvent is false, a value must be supplied for either DurationInMinutes or EndDateTime. Supplying values in both fields is allowed if the values add up to the same amount of time.Depending on your API version, errors with the DurationInMinutes and EndDateTime fields may appear in different places. Versions 38.0 and before—Errors always appear in the DurationInMinutes field. Versions 39.0 and later—If there’s no value for the DurationInMinutes field, errors appear in the EndDateTime field. Otherwise, they appear in the DurationInMinutes field.

fields.name: EndDate
fields.description: Read-only. Available in versions 46.0 and later. This field supplies the date value that appears in the EndDateTime field. This field is a date field with a timestamp that is always set to midnight in the Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) time zone.

fields.name: Description
fields.description: Contains a text description of the event. Limit: 32,000 characters.

fields.name: AccountId
fields.description: Represents the ID of the related account. The AccountId is determined as follows. If the value of WhatId is any of the following objects, then Salesforce uses that object’s AccountId. Account Opportunity Contract Custom object that is a child of Account If the value of the WhatId field is any other object, and the value of the WhoId field is a contact object, then Salesforce uses that contact’s AccountId. (If your org uses Shared Activities, Salesforce uses the AccountId of the primary contact.) Otherwise, Salesforce sets the value of the AccountId field to null. For information on IDs, see ID Field Type.

fields.name: OwnerId
fields.description: Contains the ID of the user or public calendar who owns the event. Label is Assigned to ID.

fields.name: IsPrivate
fields.description: Indicates whether users other than the creator of the event can (false) or can’t (true) see the event details when viewing the event user’s calendar. However, users with the View All Data or Modify All Data permission can see private events in reports and searches, or when viewing other users’ calendars. Private events can’t be associated with opportunities, accounts, cases, campaigns, contracts, leads, or contacts. Label is Private.

fields.name: ShowAs
fields.description: Indicates how this event appears when another user views the calendar: Busy, Out of Office, or Free. Label is Show Time As.

fields.name: IsChild
fields.description: Indicates whether the event is a child of another event (true) or not (false).

fields.name: IsGroupEvent
fields.description: Indicates whether the event is a group event—that is, whether it has invitees (true) or not (false).

fields.name: GroupEventType
fields.description: Read-only. Available in API versions 19.0 and later. The possible values are: 0 (Non–group event)—An event with no invitees. 1 (Group event)—An event with invitees. 2 (Proposed event)—An event created when a user requests a meeting with a contact, lead, or person account using the Salesforce user interface. When the user confirms the meeting, the proposed event becomes a group event. You can’t create, edit, or delete proposed events in the API. This value is no longer used in API version 41.0 and later. 3 (IsRecurrence2 Series Pattern)—An event representing an event series recurrence pattern in Lightning Experience.

fields.name: IsArchived
fields.description: Indicates whether the event has been archived.

fields.name: RecurrenceActivityId
fields.description: Read-only. Not required on create. Contains the ID of the main record of the Salesforce Classic recurring event. Subsequent occurrences have the same value in this field.

fields.name: IsRecurrence
fields.description: Indicates whether a Salesforce Classic event is scheduled to repeat itself (true) or only occurs once (false). This is a read-only field when updating records, but not when creating them. If this field value is true, then RecurrenceEndDateOnly, RecurrenceStartDateTime, RecurrenceType, and any recurrence fields associated with the given recurrence type must be populated. Label is Create recurring series of events.

fields.name: RecurrenceStartDateTime
fields.description: Indicates the date and time when the Salesforce Classic recurring event begins. The value must precede the RecurrenceEndDateOnly. The time portion of this field is always transferred in the Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) time zone. Translate the time portion to or from a local time zone for the user or the application, as appropriate.

fields.name: RecurrenceEndDateOnly
fields.description: Indicates the last date on which the event repeats. For multiday Salesforce Classic recurring events, this is the day on which the last occurrence starts. This field is a date field with a timestamp that is always set to midnight in the Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) time zone. Don’t attempt to alter the timestamp to account for time zone differences.

fields.name: RecurrenceTimeZoneSidKey
fields.description: Indicates the time zone associated with a Salesforce Classic recurring event. For example, “UTC-8:00” for Pacific Standard Time.

fields.name: RecurrenceType
fields.description: Indicates how often the Salesforce Classic event repeats. For example, daily, weekly, or every nth month (where “nth” is defined in RecurrenceInstance).

fields.name: RecurrenceInterval
fields.description: Indicates the interval between Salesforce Classic recurring events.

fields.name: RecurrenceDayOfWeekMask
fields.description: Indicates the day or days of the week on which the Salesforce Classic recurring event repeats. This field contains a bitmask. The values are as follows: Sunday = 1 Monday = 2 Tuesday = 4 Wednesday = 8 Thursday = 16 Friday = 32 Saturday = 64 Multiple days are represented as the sum of their numerical values. For example, Tuesday and Thursday = 4 + 16 = 20.

fields.name: RecurrenceDayOfMonth
fields.description: Indicates the day of the month on which the event repeats.

fields.name: RecurrenceInstance
fields.description: Indicates the frequency of the Salesforce Classic event’s recurrence. For example, 2nd or 3rd.

fields.name: RecurrenceMonthOfYear
fields.description: Indicates the month in which the Salesforce Classic recurring event repeats.

fields.name: ReminderDateTime
fields.description: Represents the time when the reminder is scheduled to fire, if IsReminderSet is set to true. If IsReminderSet is set to false, then the user may have deselected the reminder checkbox in the Salesforce user interface, or the reminder has already fired at the time indicated by the value.

fields.name: IsReminderSet
fields.description: Indicates whether the activity is a reminder (true) or not (false).

fields.name: EventSubtype
fields.description: Provides standard subtypes to facilitate creating and searching for events. This field isn’t updateable.

fields.name: IsRecurrence2Exclusion
fields.description: Read-only. This field available in API version 44.0 and later. Indicates when updates to a Lightning Experience event series recurrence pattern have been made, but affect future event occurrences only. For past event occurrences, IsRecurrence2Exclusion is set to true, excluding past occurrences from the series recurrence pattern.

fields.name: Recurrence2PatternText
fields.description: Read-only. This field available in API version 44.0 and later. Indicates the recurrence pattern for Lightning Experience event series. Recurrence2PatternText is implemented with RFC 5545 standard specifications for internet calendaring and scheduling. See Event Series section in this topic for usage examples. This field has a maximum length of 512 characters.

fields.name: Recurrence2PatternVersion
fields.description: Read-only. This field available in API version 44.0 and later. Indicates the standard specifications for Lightning Experience event series recurrence patterns. The only possible value is 1 (RFC 5545 v4 RRULE)—RFC 5545 is a standard set of specifications for internet calendaring and scheduling that IsRecurrence2 adheres to for series recurrence patterns. RFC 5545 specifications for series recurrence patterns are called rrules. For examples of rrule usage, see the Event Series section in this topic.

fields.name: IsRecurrence2
fields.description: Read-only. This field available in API version 44.0 and later. Indicates whether a Lightning Experience event is scheduled to repeat (true) or only occurs once (false. If this field value is true, then Recurrence2PatternText and Recurrence2PatternVersion must be populated. Label is Repeat.

fields.name: IsRecurrence2Exception
fields.description: Read-only. This field available in API version 44.0 and later. Indicates whether an individual event in a Lightning Experience event series has a recurrence pattern that’s different from the rest of the series, making it an exception.

fields.name: Recurrence2PatternStartDate
fields.description: Read-only. This field available in API version 44.0 and later. Indicates the date and time when the Lightning Experience event series begins. The time portion of this field is always transferred in the Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) time zone. Translate the time portion to or from a local time zone for the user or the application, as appropriate.

fields.name: Recurrence2PatternTimeZone
fields.description: This field available in API version 44.0 and later. Indicates the time zone in which the Lightning Experience event series was created or updated. This field uses standard Java TimeZone IDs. For example, America/Los_Angeles.

typeDefs.name: EventSObject
typeDefs.description: Represents an event in the calendar. In the user interface, event and task records are collectively referred to as activities.

fields.name: Name
fields.description: Optional. A label for the condition.

fields.name: FilterTarget
fields.description: Required. The target object or field used in the condition. For example, to create a condition that applies to new cases, use Case.Status as the FilterTarget.

fields.name: FilterTargetValue
fields.description: Optional. The value that’s compared to the value of the FilterTarget. For example, to create a condition that applies to new cases, use New as the FilterTargetValue.

fields.name: Operation
fields.description: Required. Specifies the operator used to compare the target field and the target value. For example, to create a condition that applies to new cases, use EQUALS for the Operation field, as in Case.Status EQUALS New. EQUALS NOTEQUALS CONTAINS NOTCONTAIN

fields.name: SortOrder
fields.description: Required. The order in which the criteria are evaluated.

fields.name: ExpressionFilterId
fields.description: Required. The ID of the ExpressionFilter object that references this condition.

typeDefs.name: ExpressionFilterCriteriaSObject
typeDefs.description: Represents a condition in an expression that’s used to control the execution of macro instructions.

fields.name: Name
fields.description: Optional. A label for the expression.

fields.name: FilterConditionLogic
fields.description: Optional. The filter conditions to use and the order in which to apply them. For example, ‘1 AND 2’ evaluates condition 1 and then condition 2.

fields.name: ContextId
fields.description: Required. The ID of the MacroInstruction object that contains the expression.

fields.name: FilterDescription
fields.description: Optional. A description of the filter expression that helps to explain the logic to users. For example, ‘Applies to New cases.’

typeDefs.name: ExpressionFilterSObject
typeDefs.description: Represents a logical expression that’s used to control the execution of macro instructions.

fields.name: DeveloperName
fields.description: The unique name of the object in the API. This name can contain only underscores and alphanumeric characters, and must be unique in your org. It must begin with a letter, not include spaces, not end with an underscore, and not contain two consecutive underscores. In managed packages, this field prevents naming conflicts on package installations. With this field, a developer can change the object’s name in a managed package and the changes are reflected in a subscriber’s organization.When creating large sets of data, always specify a unique DeveloperName for each record. If no DeveloperName is specified, performance may slow while Salesforce generates one for each record.

fields.name: Language
fields.description: The language of the MasterLabel.

fields.name: MasterLabel
fields.description: Master label for the external data source. This internal label doesn’t get translated.

fields.name: NamespacePrefix
fields.description: The namespace prefix that is associated with this object. Each Developer Edition org that creates a managed package has a unique namespace prefix. Limit: 15 characters. You can refer to a component in a managed package by using the namespacePrefix__componentName notation.

fields.name: Type
fields.description: Specifies the adapter that connects to the external system.

fields.name: Endpoint
fields.description: The URL of the external system, or if that URL is defined in a named credential, the named credential URL.

fields.name: Repository
fields.description: Used for SharePoint Online. An optional name of the repository in the data source. Not applicable to all data source types.

fields.name: PrincipalType
fields.description: Specifies whether the org uses one set (NamedUser), multiple sets (PerUser), or no (Anonymous) credentials to access the external system. Each set of credentials corresponds to a login account on the external system. Corresponds to Identity Type in the user interface.

fields.name: Protocol
fields.description: Specifies whether to use OAuth, password authentication, or no authentication to access the external system.

fields.name: AuthProviderId
fields.description: Salesforce ID of the authentication provider, which defines the service that provides the login process and approves access to the external system. Only users with the “Customize Application” and “Manage AuthProviders” permissions can view this field. This field is available in API version 39.0 and later.

fields.name: CustomConfiguration
fields.description: A JSON-encoded configuration string that defines parameters specific to the type of external data source.

typeDefs.name: ExternalDataSourceSObject
typeDefs.description: Represents an external data source, which defines connection details for integration with data and content that are stored outside the Salesforce org.

fields.name: ExternalDataSourceId
fields.description: Salesforce ID of the external data source or named credential that defines the external system.

fields.name: UserId
fields.description: ID of the Salesforce user who’s accessing the external system.

fields.name: Protocol
fields.description: Specifies whether to use OAuth, password authentication, or no authentication when the user accesses the external system.

fields.name: Username
fields.description: Username portion of the credentials for the Salesforce user to access the external system.

fields.name: Password
fields.description: Password portion of the credentials for the Salesforce user to access the external system.

fields.name: AuthProviderId
fields.description: Salesforce ID of the authentication provider, which defines the service that provides the login process and approves access to the external system. Only users with the “Customize Application” and “Manage AuthProviders” permissions can view this field. This field is available in API version 39.0 and later.

typeDefs.name: ExternalDataUserAuthSObject
typeDefs.description: Stores authentication settings for a Salesforce user to access an external system. The external system must be defined in an external data source or a named credential that’s configured to use per-user authentication.

fields.name: FeedEntityId
fields.description: The ID of the associated feed entity that contains this attachment.

fields.name: Type
fields.description: The type of this feed attachment. Valid values are: 0 Content—A content attachment. 1 InlineImage—An inline image. The system creates an inline image attachment when an image is added to the body of the associated FeedItem. You can’t add an inline image directly using FeedAttachment. 2 Link—A link. 3 FeedEntity—A feed entity, for example, a post that is shared. Available in API version 39 and later in Lightning Experience. 4 ChatterExtension—a Rich Publisher App that’s integrated with the Chatter publisher. 5 Record—A record.

fields.name: RecordId
fields.description: The ID of the record that this feed attachment contains. For inline images, RecordId is a ContentDocument ID. For content attachments, RecordId is a ContentVersion ID, For feed items, RecordId is a FeedItem ID.

fields.name: Title
fields.description: The title of this feed attachment. When Type is Link, Title value is the label for the attachment link. Otherwise, Title value isn’t used.

fields.name: Value
fields.description: The string value of this FeedAttachment. This field is optional. If the feed attachment is a Link FeedAttachment, the value is the link URL string.

typeDefs.name: FeedAttachmentSObject
typeDefs.description: Represents an attachment to a feed item, such as a file attachment or a link. Use FeedAttachment to add various attachments to one feed item.

fields.name: FeedItemId
fields.description: ID of the feed item containing the comment.

fields.name: ParentId
fields.description: ID of a record associated with the feed comment. For example, if you are commenting on a change to a field on Account, ParentId is set to the account ID.

fields.name: SystemModstamp
fields.description: Date and time when a user or automated process (such as a trigger) last modified this record. In this context, \"trigger\" refers to Salesforce code that runs to implement standard functionality, and not an Apex trigger. SystemModstamp is a read-only system field, available in FeedComment as of API version 37.0.

fields.name: Revision
fields.description: The number of times the comment was revised.

fields.name: LastEditById
fields.description: ID of the user who last edited the feed comment.

fields.name: LastEditDate
fields.description: The date the feed comment was last edited.

fields.name: CommentBody
fields.description: The text in the comment.

fields.name: InsertedById
fields.description: ID of the user who added this item to the feed. For example, if an application migrates posts and comments from another application into a feed, the InsertedBy value is set to the ID of the context user.

fields.name: CommentType
fields.description: The type of comment: ContentComment—an uploaded file on a comment TextComment—a direct text entry on a comment Before API version 24.0, a text entry was required on a comment. As of version 24.0, a text entry is optional if the CommentType is ContentComment.

fields.name: RelatedRecordId
fields.description: ID of the ContentVersion record associated with a ContentComment. This field is null for all comments except ContentComment. For example, set this field to an existing ContentVersion ID and set the CommentType to ContentComment.

fields.name: IsRichText
fields.description:
Indicates whether the feed CommentBody contains rich text. If you post a rich text feed comment using SOAP API, set IsRichText to true and escape HTML entities from the body. Otherwise, the comment is rendered as plain text. Rich text supports the following HTML tags:

Though the
